# Session handoff: v1.3, after the Week 7 close (2026-11-28)

> **What this is.** A save point for the session of 2026-11-27/28. Check it against GitHub
> before acting: the remote is the truth, this file is the map.
>
> **State at the end of the session:** `main` at `eb62d198e` (docs: close v1.3 Week 7, #2765).
> **0 open PRs. 0 open Dependabot PRs. Milestone 34 (Week 7) closed.** 44 open issues: Week 8
> (milestone 35) 22, `v1.3 Backlog` 22.

## RESUME HERE

1. **Week 8 is the last week of the cycle, due 2026-11-29**: test and dependency debt, decisions,
   and the cycle close. Earlier cycles closed with a frozen ledger
   (`docs/progress-v1.N.md`), a retro (`docs/retro-v1.N.md`), a `v1.N.0` tag and GitHub release,
   and the CLAUDE.md §13 headline. Check milestone 35 for what is open; each item ends shipped
   or rolled by name with a reason.
2. **The CI speed-up is half done**: branch `perf/ci-faster-backend-and-e2e` at `5d637bf2c`,
   pushed, **no PR yet**. See "CI speed-up" below for what is done, what is measured, and the two
   flakes left before it can merge.
3. **#2766** (Week 8): the first weekly cross-browser run's findings.

## What this session did

### Dependabot: all closed

- Merged as proposed: #2707, #2708, #2709, #2711, #2717, #2719, #2742, #2745, #2746, #2747, #2750,
  and #2748 (FastAPI 0.142 → 0.165).
- #2748 was merged after reading the release notes: no `Form()`, query/header parameter models or
  `root_path` in DataQ, and CI's spec-drift check showed `openapi.json` unchanged.
- #2718, #2715 and #2713 each conflicted in `pnpm-lock.yaml` after the one before merged, and
  Dependabot answered neither `rebase` nor `recreate`. Their exact bumps landed in **#2758**
  (one pnpm-resolved lockfile), and all three were closed as superseded.
- #2710 (celery 5.7 alone) could never resolve: kombu 5.7 needs redis-py ≥6.4, and dependabot.yml
  ignores redis majors. Superseded by **#2744** (celery 5.7.0 + redis-py 7.4.1, #2743). The
  `types-redis` stubs were dropped (redis-py ships its own types). A retry-default probe showed
  that our `from_url` clients don't amplify timeouts.
- #2733 (picomatch audit) closed as not planned: the advisory GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf was withdrawn
  upstream.

### Week 7: closed 2026-11-28 (six days late, nothing rolled; ledger in #2765)

| Issue | PR | Note |
|---|---|---|
| #2724 one answer to "needs a stored secret?" | #2749 | Didn't follow the issue's sketch: counting `catalog_secret_name` would have flagged a catalog-password-only REST catalog as missing its credential |
| #2751 observed_value sweep never used its index | #2752 | **Live bug found during #2729**: SQLAlchemy renders `col["k"]` as a JSONB subscript, and the index uses `->`. Rule recorded in the audit page |
| #2729 literals for index constants + real-statement audit | #2754 | `backend/app/db/literals.py: sql_constant()`; the audit compiles real statements with the psycopg3 dialect |
| #2725 daily reconcile of result_status_hourly | #2755 | Delta repair, not overwrite; a two-connection test fails on the naive version. Log event `result_rollup_drift_repaired` (no ops metrics pipeline exists) |
| #2632 Azure stack on an empty subscription | #2757, #2760 | `create_shared_resources` (default true). Mocked `tofu test` + new `opentofu.yml` workflow. Live plan added to #2224. **Existing Azure deployments must set it false before their next plan** |
| #2662 weekly Firefox + WebKit lane | #2761, #2764 | Mondays 05:17 UTC + manual dispatch, inside the E2E job, reseeding per browser. The Firefox crash is axe-core's (#2759), and the trend drawer's scan is skipped on Firefox only |
| #2633 + #2398 screenshots and clips | #2762 | All 23 screenshots + 9 clips. The capture lane gained a local PG warehouse (:55433), a Celery worker and `shrink-screenshots.sh`. The suite panel is now **Alerting** in the UI and the docs |
| #2763 weekly CI run blockers | #2764 | E2E timeout 60 min on schedule/dispatch. The secret scan's `logopts=-1` was a `git rev-list` usage error (it also broke branch-creating pushes) |

Also merged early in the session (from the 2026-11-18 handoff): #2721, #2726, #2728, #2731,
#2732, #2734, #2735, #2736, #2738, #2740, #2741.

### Filed and still open

- **#2766** (Week 8): the cross-browser run. `admin.spec.ts:371` (transfer then delete) fails on
  Firefox and WebKit: pressing Enter in the owner picker doesn't select, so Transfer stays
  disabled. It also fails locally on macOS on all three browsers, while Chromium passes in CI.
  First check whether a real keyboard user can pick an owner on those browsers. WebKit flakes:
  `check-editor.spec.ts:113` and `suites.spec.ts:58`.
- **#2753** (Week 8): the rollup sweep tests and `test_dashboard_one_pass` fail after
  `backend/tests/db` in the same session. `roll_up_pending(limit=2)` returned 3. Undetermined
  whether that's leftover rows or the `UPDATE … WHERE id IN (SELECT … LIMIT n FOR UPDATE SKIP
  LOCKED)` claim taking more than `n` (which would be a product bug). Also blocks the CI speed-up.
- #2756 (backlog): an admin command for a full recount of `result_status_hourly`.
- #2759 (backlog): axe-core's scan of the trend drawer crashes Firefox; the bisect notes are in
  the issue.

## CI speed-up (branch `perf/ci-faster-backend-and-e2e`, WIP)

The user asked for this: "Backend — tests" and "Frontend — browser E2E" each take over 10 min.

**Measured** (CI run 46059360413): backend `pytest` 677 s serially. E2E: static demo
(record 2.8 min + smoke 2.5 min) 322 s, Playwright specs 333 s (`workers: 1`). Locally the backend
suite is 348 s serial vs **~131 s with `-n 4 --dist loadfile`**, with coverage unchanged at 97.19%.

**On the branch:**
- `pytest-xdist==3.8.0` (MIT; dependency execnet MIT) in `backend/requirements-dev.txt`. CI runs
  `pytest backend/tests/ -n 4 --dist loadfile`.
- `backend/tests/conftest.py`: each xdist worker gets its own DB (`<name>_gwN`, created via the
  server's `postgres` DB) and its own Redis index. `structlog.configure` is wrapped so tests
  never cache loggers: cached loggers hid lines from `capture_logs` depending on test order
  (26 files use it).
- Two test fixes: `test_trigger_labels.py` (`uuid4()` param ids made workers collect different
  tests) and `test_secrets.py::test_approle_403_relogin_is_compare_and_swap_under_concurrency`
  (the handler refused every token, so the count tracked scheduling; now only the cached one is
  revoked and `logins == 2`). **That second fix still needs a mutation check**: with an
  unconditional clear in `_forget_token_if_current` it must fail.
- Backend checkout `filter: blob:none` (was 64 s with `fetch-depth: 0`).
- E2E: the static demo moved to a new job, **`frontend-demo`** ("Frontend — static demo (record,
  build, smoke)"), sharing the E2E job's services/env/setup steps through YAML anchors.
  `publish-demo` now `needs: frontend-demo`. Required check names are unchanged.

**Before it can merge:** three local `-n 4` runs each failed one different existing test.
1. `test_secrets` CAS: fixed (above).
2. `test_dashboard_one_pass[partly in the summary-*]`: `pending_count` 0, the #2753 symptom. Fix
   #2753 first.
3. `test_markers.py::test_marker_lookups_use_the_expression_index` and
   `test_runs_triggered_by_index_migration.py::test_pipeline_run_marker_lookup_still_uses_the_expression_index`:
   the planner picks `uq_pipeline_runs_provider_run` (unique, which `drop_rival_indexes` spares) or
   `ix_pipeline_runs_provider_pipeline` (`test_markers` doesn't drop rivals; #2739). Likely fix:
   let `tests/support/index_plans.py: drop_rival_indexes` also drop non-PK unique indexes and
   constraints (opt-in), and use it in both.

Then: three or more clean local `-n 4` runs, a PR, and confirm the timings in CI. Also consider
splitting the demo record/smoke route walk across 2–3 pages (each walks 69 routes serially).
A YAML anchor in `ci.yml` is new for this repo; the PR's CI proves the runner accepts it.

## Working notes for the next session

- **Shared conda env `dataq`** now matches `main`'s pins (celery 5.7.0, redis 7.4.1, FastAPI
  0.165, pytest 9.2.0, alembic 1.20.1, pytest-xdist 3.8.0) and `types-redis` is uninstalled.
  The pre-commit mypy and licence hooks refuse a commit when the env drifts from the pins: run
  `pip install -r backend/requirements-dev.txt` in it after any dependency merge.
- **Docker Desktop** was started this session, and the contributor compose stack is up (it
  restarted itself). The capture stack and its warehouse container are destroyed, and Ollama is
  stopped. Port 5433 belongs to the harness warehouse; the capture warehouse uses 55433.
- **Capture lane:** `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME=dataq scripts/docs/capture-stack.sh start` when run from
  a worktree (compose otherwise derives another project name). Run Playwright directly, not via
  `capture-stack.sh capture` with a file filter (`--project docs-capture "$@"` takes the file as a
  project name). Ollama with `qwen2.5:14b` for the LLM captures. Run
  `scripts/docs/shrink-screenshots.sh` after capturing.
- **Merging:** `gh pr merge --auto` merges at once if the checks are already green
  (`strict=false`). A stacked PR's auto-merge targets the parent branch: arm it only after the
  base merges and GitHub retargets it. Unresolved review threads block a merge with every check
  green (that's what held #2731).
- **Changelog check** reads the `no-changelog` label from the event payload: re-running an old
  run keeps failing, so toggle the label to get a fresh event.
- **Never close superseded PRs before the replacement exists** (this session did, then corrected
  the comments on #2718/#2715/#2713).
- Run `tofu fmt -check` after the last edit, not before it (#2760).
- The Entire Gates check is red on every PR and isn't required; ignore it.
- The GitHub MCP server's token is expired (`AUTH_HEADER_REJECTED`); `gh` CLI works.

<browser_instruction># Claude in Chrome browser automation

You have access to browser automation tools (mcp__claude-in-chrome__*) for interacting with web pages in Chrome. Follow these guidelines for effective browser automation.

## Loading deferred tools

If the mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load every tool you expect to need in ONE ToolSearch call — the select query accepts a comma-separated list — never one call per tool. Start with the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting.

## GIF recording

When performing multi-step browser interactions that the user may want to review or share, use mcp__claude-in-chrome__gif_creator to record them.

You must ALWAYS:
* Capture extra frames before and after taking actions to ensure smooth playback
* Name the file meaningfully to help the user identify it later (e.g., "login_process.gif")

## Console log debugging

You can use mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages to read console output. Console output may be verbose. If you are looking for specific log entries, use the 'pattern' parameter with a regex-compatible pattern. This filters results efficiently and avoids overwhelming output. For example, use pattern: "[MyApp]" to filter for application-specific logs rather than reading all console output.

## Alerts and dialogs

IMPORTANT: Do not trigger JavaScript alerts, confirms, prompts, or browser modal dialogs through your actions. These browser dialogs block all further browser events and will prevent the extension from receiving any subsequent commands. Instead, when possible, use console.log for debugging and then use the mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages tool to read those log messages. If a page has dialog-triggering elements:
1. Avoid clicking buttons or links that may trigger alerts (e.g., "Delete" buttons with confirmation dialogs)
2. If you must interact with such elements, warn the user first that this may interrupt the session
3. Use mcp__claude-in-chrome__javascript_tool to check for and dismiss any existing dialogs before proceeding

If you accidentally trigger a dialog and lose responsiveness, inform the user they need to manually dismiss it in the browser.

## Avoid rabbit holes and loops

When using browser automation tools, stay focused on the specific task. If you encounter any of the following, stop and ask the user for guidance:
- Unexpected complexity or tangential browser exploration
- Browser tool calls failing or returning errors after 2-3 attempts
- No response from the browser extension
- Page elements not responding to clicks or input
- Pages not loading or timing out
- Unable to complete the browser task despite multiple approaches

Explain what you attempted, what went wrong, and ask how the user would like to proceed. Do not keep retrying the same failing browser action or explore unrelated pages without checking in first.

## Tab context and session startup

IMPORTANT: At the start of each browser automation session, call mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp first to get information about the user's current browser tabs. Use this context to understand what the user might want to work with before creating new tabs.

Never reuse tab IDs from a previous/other session. Follow these guidelines:
1. Only reuse an existing tab if the user explicitly asks to work with it
2. Otherwise, create a new tab with mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp
3. If a tool returns an error indicating the tab doesn't exist or is invalid, call tabs_context_mcp to get fresh tab IDs
4. When a tab is closed by the user or a navigation error occurs, call tabs_context_mcp to see what tabs are available</browser_instruction>

---
name: dev-branch-pruning-technique
description: How to safely bulk-prune worktrees/local branches in this squash-merge-only repo, and the same-session Docker container/image/build-cache cleanup — what's safe to remove vs what backs the live dev stack
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 23338a22-3fe4-41f8-b4f7-1c7ba861cfd6
  modified: 2026-08-09T20:02:13.690Z
---

Ran a full worktree/branch/cache cleanup 2026-08-09 (60+ stale worktrees and local branches had accumulated from many sessions' `Agent(isolation: "worktree")` calls). The technique, since **this repo squash-merges exclusively** (CONTRIBUTING.md rule), so `git branch --merged main` is useless — a squash-merged branch's original commits never become ancestors of `main`, so they always show as "not merged" even when fully landed:

1. `git worktree list` → for each non-main worktree, `git -C <path> status --short` (confirm no uncommitted work) before removing anything.
2. For each worktree's branch, check `git ls-remote --heads origin <branch>` — **empty = the remote branch is gone**, which in this repo only happens after `gh pr merge --delete-branch`, i.e. strong evidence it's safe. Spot-check a handful via `gh pr list --state merged --head <branch>` to confirm (don't trust the heuristic blind for the whole batch, but no need to check every single one either).
3. `git worktree remove <path> --force` for each confirmed-safe worktree, then `git branch -D <branch>`.
4. After worktrees are gone, the repo usually has MORE orphan local branches than worktrees (scratch branches like `pr-1220-a`..`pr-1220-e`, `worktree-agent-<id>` stubs, etc. that never had their own worktree). Same remote-gone check applies; a `git log main..<branch> --oneline | wc -l` count of "N commits not in main" is EXPECTED and not a red flag for these (squash-merge again) — the real safety net is the remote-gone + spot-checked-merged-PR evidence, not the ahead-count.
5. `git remote prune origin` to drop stale `origin/*` remote-tracking refs for branches already deleted on GitHub.
6. **Never touch `entire/*` branches** (e.g. `entire/checkpoints/v1`) even though they look like leftover branches — they're the `entire` checkpoint/session-history tool's own state (see the `entire-search` agent), not feature work. One of them (`entire/checkpoints/v1`) still has a live remote counterpart; leave both local `entire/*` refs alone.
7. `git gc --prune=now` afterward to reclaim space from the deleted branches' now-unreachable objects — `--aggressive` is expensive and can blow past a 2-minute tool timeout on a repo this size (30k+ objects); plain `--prune=now` is enough and finishes fast. Verify with `git count-objects -vH` (want `garbage: 0` / `prune-packable: 0`) and `git fsck --no-progress` (want no error/missing/corrupt lines) after, not just trust the timeout didn't corrupt anything.

Also cleared regenerable local caches (`__pycache__`, `.pytest_cache`, `.mypy_cache` — both repo-root and `backend/`, `.ruff_cache`, `.coverage`, `frontend/coverage`, `frontend/node_modules/.vite`) — all gitignored/untracked, confirmed via `git status --short` before deleting, safe to nuke anytime.

## Docker container/image/cache cleanup (same session, 2026-08-09)

The local dev stack is `docker compose -f docker-compose.yml` (7 services: `api`, `worker`, `frontend`, `postgres`, `redis`, `openbao`, `mailpit` — the ADR-0032/0039 local stack). **Never remove containers/images backing a currently-running `docker compose ps` service** — check that first, every time. `redis:7-alpine` in particular is a **standing security-pin, not a version to "helpfully" bump** — see [[project_redis7_pin_is_a_security_gate]].

What accumulates as genuine test cruft and is safe to remove, by category:
- **One-off `docker run` containers**, not part of any compose project — this session had `test-pg-1197`/`test-pg-1199`/`test-pg-aef7256` (scratch Postgres instances spun up for parallel-worktree test runs, named after the issue/agent-id, on non-5432 ports). Identify via `docker ps -a` naming that doesn't match a compose service, and a port mapping that ISN'T the compose stack's own port.
- **Exited containers from a deleted worktree's own local compose project** (`agent-<id>-openbao-1`, `agent-<id>-redis-1`, etc.) — the worktree is already gone (see branch-pruning above), so these are pure orphans.
- **Harness-local containers** (`dataq-harness-local-*` — Airflow webserver/worker/scheduler/init, fakesnow, MinIO, their own Postgres/Redis) — all recreatable via the harness repo's own compose file; safe to remove once stopped and not actively being used for a harness test window.
- **Superseded local image builds and old registry pulls** not referenced by any current container: old `dataq1150-*`/`dataq-otp-mail-secret` variant images, unpinned `postgres:16`/`postgres:14` (compose uses `postgres:16-alpine` specifically), `ghcr.io/theurgicduke771/dataq-{backend,frontend}` old pulled tags (rebuilt locally instead), `dataqacr3erlgd.azurecr.io/*` harness images, unpinned `nginx:alpine` (the frontend Dockerfile pins `nginx:1.27-alpine` specifically — that tag stays, the bare one doesn't), and generic debugging images (`traefik/whoami`, `mendhak/http-https-echo`, bare `ubuntu`/`python:3-alpine`/`alpine`) that clearly aren't part of any DataQ path.
- **`moby/buildkit:buildx-stable-1`** — only actually needed if a buildx builder uses the `docker-container` driver; check `docker buildx ls` first, and if every builder shows driver `docker` (not `docker-container`), this image is dangling cruft from a one-off invocation.
- **Before removing anything ambiguous** (e.g. `koalaman/shellcheck`, `ghcr.io/betterleaks/betterleaks`), grep `.pre-commit-config.yaml` and `.github/workflows/` for actual usage — betterleaks IS a live pre-commit hook dependency (kept), shellcheck was only referenced via inline `# shellcheck disable=` comments, never actually invoked as a tool (removed).
- **Leave unrelated personal containers/images alone** (this machine also runs `embyserver`/`jellyfin` media servers, nothing to do with DataQ) — don't touch anything outside the project's own naming/purpose just because it showed up in `docker ps -a`.

Cleanup order: `docker rm -f` the identified containers first, THEN `docker rmi` the now-unreferenced images (an image with a container still on it, even stopped, can't be removed), THEN `docker volume prune -f` (only removes volumes with ZERO container references, running or stopped — safe by construction, but eyeball `docker volume ls` first for anything that looks like a real named data volume you'd want to keep, e.g. `dataq_postgres_data`), THEN `docker builder prune -f` (build-cache layers — this is usually the SINGLE BIGGEST reclaim, tens of GB from repeated local `docker build`/`docker compose build` runs; fully safe, just makes the next build slower). Verify nothing broke with `docker compose ps` afterward — every service should still show `Up`/`healthy`.

## 2026-11-08 additions

- **zsh: never name a loop variable `path`** — it is tied to `PATH`, so `while read path …` empties the command search path and every command in the loop fails with "command not found".
- **Ignored files are not all disposable.** `git clean -X` would delete `.env*`, `.entire/`, `.claude/settings.local.json`, `.vscode/` and the ignored lineage fixture captures. Remove caches by name instead (`__pycache__`, `.mypy_cache`, `.ruff_cache`, `.coverage`, `frontend/dist*`, `tsconfig.tsbuildinfo`, `frontend/e2e/.role-tokens.json`).
- **Scratch databases accumulate on the dev Postgres** (`dataq_test_<issue>`, `dataq_perf_<n>`, `dataq_mig_<n>`, …). Keep `dataq`, `dataq_test`, `dataq_docs`, `dataq_perf`, `iceberg_catalog`; check `git grep -w <name>` before dropping any other. Dropping a database needs the user's explicit go-ahead (the auto-mode classifier blocks it otherwise).

5. `git remote prune origin` to drop stale `origin/*` remote-tracking refs for branches already deleted on GitHub.
6. **Never touch `entire/*` branches** (e.g. `entire/checkpoints/v1`) even though they look like leftover branches — they're the `entire` checkpoint/session-history tool's own state (see the `entire-search` agent), not feature work. One of them (`entire/checkpoints/v1`) still has a live remote counterpart; leave both local `entire/*` refs alone.
7. `git gc --prune=now` afterward to reclaim space from the deleted branches' now-unreachable objects — `--aggressive` is expensive and can blow past a 2-minute tool timeout on a repo this size (30k+ objects); plain `--prune=now` is enough and finishes fast. Verify with `git count-objects -vH` (want `garbage: 0` / `prune-packable: 0`) and `git fsck --no-progress` (want no error/missing/corrupt lines) after, not just trust the timeout didn't corrupt anything.

Also cleared regenerable local caches (`__pycache__`, `.pytest_cache`, `.mypy_cache` — both repo-root and `backend/`, `.ruff_cache`, `.coverage`, `frontend/coverage`, `frontend/node_modules/.vite`) — all gitignored/untracked, confirmed via `git status --short` before deleting, safe to nuke anytime.

## Docker container/image/cache cleanup (same session, 2026-08-09)

The local dev stack is `docker compose -f docker-compose.yml` (7 services: `api`, `worker`, `frontend`, `postgres`, `redis`, `openbao`, `mailpit` — the ADR-0032/0039 local stack). **Never remove containers/images backing a currently-running `docker compose ps` service** — check that first, every time. `redis:7-alpine` in particular is a **standing security-pin, not a version to "helpfully" bump** — see [[project_redis7_pin_is_a_security_gate]].

What accumulates as genuine test cruft and is safe to remove, by category:
- **One-off `docker run` containers**, not part of any compose project — this session had `test-pg-1197`/`test-pg-1199`/`test-pg-aef7256` (scratch Postgres instances spun up for parallel-worktree test runs, named after the issue/agent-id, on non-5432 ports). Identify via `docker ps -a` naming that doesn't match a compose service, and a port mapping that ISN'T the compose stack's own port.
- **Exited containers from a deleted worktree's own local compose project** (`agent-<id>-openbao-1`, `agent-<id>-redis-1`, etc.) — the worktree is already gone (see branch-pruning above), so these are pure orphans.
- **Harness-local containers** (`dataq-harness-local-*` — Airflow webserver/worker/scheduler/init, fakesnow, MinIO, their own Postgres/Redis) — all recreatable via the harness repo's own compose file; safe to remove once stopped and not actively being used for a harness test window.
- **Superseded local image builds and old registry pulls** not referenced by any current container: old `dataq1150-*`/`dataq-otp-mail-secret` variant images, unpinned `postgres:16`/`postgres:14` (compose uses `postgres:16-alpine` specifically), `ghcr.io/theurgicduke771/dataq-{backend,frontend}` old pulled tags (rebuilt locally instead), `dataqacr3erlgd.azurecr.io/*` harness images, unpinned `nginx:alpine` (the frontend Dockerfile pins `nginx:1.27-alpine` specifically — that tag stays, the bare one doesn't), and generic debugging images (`traefik/whoami`, `mendhak/http-https-echo`, bare `ubuntu`/`python:3-alpine`/`alpine`) that clearly aren't part of any DataQ path.
- **`moby/buildkit:buildx-stable-1`** — only actually needed if a buildx builder uses the `docker-container` driver; check `docker buildx ls` first, and if every builder shows driver `docker` (not `docker-container`), this image is dangling cruft from a one-off invocation.
- **Before removing anything ambiguous** (e.g. `koalaman/shellcheck`, `ghcr.io/betterleaks/betterleaks`), grep `.pre-commit-config.yaml` and `.github/workflows/` for actual usage — betterleaks IS a live pre-commit hook dependency (kept), shellcheck was only referenced via inline `# shellcheck disable=` comments, never actually invoked as a tool (removed).
- **Leave unrelated personal containers/images alone** (this machine also runs `embyserver`/`jellyfin` media servers, nothing to do with DataQ) — don't touch anything outside the project's own naming/purpose just because it showed up in `docker ps -a`.

Cleanup order: `docker rm -f` the identified containers first, THEN `docker rmi` the now-unreferenced images (an image with a container still on it, even stopped, can't be removed), THEN `docker volume prune -f` (only removes volumes with ZERO container references, running or stopped — safe by construction, but eyeball `docker volume ls` first for anything that looks like a real named data volume you'd want to keep, e.g. `dataq_postgres_data`), THEN `docker builder prune -f` (build-cache layers — this is usually the SINGLE BIGGEST reclaim, tens of GB from repeated local `docker build`/`docker compose build` runs; fully safe, just makes the next build slower). Verify nothing broke with `docker compose ps` afterward — every service should still show `Up`/`healthy`.

## 2026-11-08 additions

- **zsh: never name a loop variable `path`** — it is tied to `PATH`, so `while read path …` empties the command search path and every command in the loop fails with "command not found".
- **Ignored files are not all disposable.** `git clean -X` would delete `.env*`, `.entire/`, `.claude/settings.local.json`, `.vscode/` and the ignored lineage fixture captures. Remove caches by name instead (`__pycache__`, `.mypy_cache`, `.ruff_cache`, `.coverage`, `frontend/dist*`, `tsconfig.tsbuildinfo`, `frontend/e2e/.role-tokens.json`).
- **Scratch databases accumulate on the dev Postgres** (`dataq_test_<issue>`, `dataq_perf_<n>`, `dataq_mig_<n>`, …). Keep `dataq`, `dataq_test`, `dataq_docs`, `dataq_perf`, `iceberg_catalog`; check `git grep -w <name>` before dropping any other. Dropping a database needs the user's explicit go-ahead (the auto-mode classifier blocks it otherwise).

WITH claimed AS (
    UPDATE runs SET results_rolled_up_at = now()
    WHERE {which}
    RETURNING id, suite_id
), added AS (
    INSERT INTO result_status_hourly (suite_id, hour, status, n)
    SELECT c.suite_id, date_trunc('hour', r.created_at, 'UTC'), r.status, count(*)
    FROM results r JOIN claimed c ON c.id = r.run_id
    GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
    ORDER BY 1, 2, 3
    ON CONFLICT (suite_id, hour, status) DO UPDATE SET n = result_status_hourly.n + EXCLUDED.n
    RETURNING 1
)
SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM claimed) AS runs
"""

    _ADD_SQL.format(which="id = :run_id AND status = 'succeeded' AND results_rolled_up_at IS NULL")
)
_ADD_PENDING = text(
    _ADD_SQL.format(

# the results of runs already added: a run not added yet has nothing to take back.

# the marker read below final: a sweep that has claimed one of them has not committed, and
# this waits for it, then sees its marker and subtracts what it added.
_LOCK_RUNS = text("""
    SELECT id FROM runs
    WHERE status = 'succeeded'
      AND id IN (SELECT run_id FROM results WHERE check_id = ANY (CAST(:check_ids AS uuid[])))
    ORDER BY id
    FOR UPDATE

_LOCK_BUCKETS = text("""
    SELECT 1 FROM result_status_hourly h
    JOIN (
        SELECT run.suite_id, date_trunc('hour', r.created_at, 'UTC') AS hour, r.status
        FROM results r JOIN runs run ON run.id = r.run_id

    ORDER BY h.suite_id, h.hour, h.status
    FOR UPDATE OF h
    """)

    SET n = h.n - gone.n

def roll_up_run(session: Session, run_id: uuid.UUID) -> bool:
    """Add a just-succeeded run's results to the table, in the caller's transaction.

    Inside a savepoint, and never raises: a failure here must not fail the run. The run then
    stays un-added, readers go on counting it from `results`, and the sweep adds it later.
    Returns whether the add ran without error.
    """
    try:
        with session.begin_nested():
            session.execute(_ADD_ONE, {"run_id": run_id})
    except Exception:
        log.exception("result_rollup_failed", run_id=str(run_id))
        return False
    return True

    """Add up to ``limit`` (default ``SWEEP_BATCH``) succeeded runs not added yet, oldest id
    first; commits. Returns how many were added: 0 means nothing is left to claim.

    One statement for the batch. If it fails, the runs are added one at a time instead, each
    in its own savepoint, so one run that cannot be added (and is logged) does not hold the
    rest of the backlog back.
    """
    wanted = limit or SWEEP_BATCH
    try:
        with session.begin_nested():
            added = int(session.execute(_ADD_PENDING, {"limit": wanted}).scalar_one())
    except Exception:
        log.exception("result_rollup_batch_failed", limit=wanted)
        ids = session.scalars(unrolled_runs_statement(wanted)).all()
        added = sum(roll_up_run(session, run_id) for run_id in ids)
    session.commit()
    return added

        SELECT suite_id, hour, status, n FROM result_status_hourly

    )

           coalesce(c.status, h.status) AS status
    FROM counted c FULL JOIN held h
      ON h.suite_id = c.suite_id AND h.hour = c.hour AND h.status = c.status
    WHERE coalesce(c.n, 0) <> coalesce(h.n, 0)
    ORDER BY 1, 2, 3
    """)
_LOCK_DRIFTED = text("""
    SELECT 1 FROM result_status_hourly h
    repaired = [
        Drift(row.suite_id, row.hour, row.status, int(row.held), int(row.counted))
        for row in session.execute(_REPAIR, keys)
    ]
    session.commit()
    return repaired

    """Succeeded runs not in the table yet."""

    session.rollback()

    same transaction: the delete cascades to the results this reads."""
    if not check_ids:

    params = {"check_ids": [str(i) for i in check_ids]}
    session.execute(_LOCK_RUNS, params)
    session.execute(_LOCK_BUCKETS, params)
    session.execute(_FORGET_CHECKS, params)

**Fix:** point `AWS_CONFIG_FILE` and `AWS_SHARED_CREDENTIALS_FILE` at an empty file for the test session (an autouse fixture in `backend/tests/conftest.py`), so no test reads the developer's AWS files.

**Acceptance**
- [ ] the two tests pass with an `s3` section present in `~/.aws/config`
- [ ] the ambient-config behaviour is either documented or switched off

      - dependency-name: sqlalchemy

          - version-update:semver-major
    groups:
      # The OTel SDK and its instrumentations pin each other exactly (sdk 1.N needs
      # semantic-conventions 0.Nb0, which instrumentation 0.Nb0 also pins), so a lone bump is
      # ResolutionImpossible (#2184). One PR moves them together. The Azure exporter must ride
      # along: 1.0.0b57 requires opentelemetry-sdk~=1.44.0, so the SDK can only move once an
      # exporter release accepts the new minor — until then the grouped PR fails CI, not prod.
      opentelemetry:
        patterns:
          - opentelemetry-*
          - azure-monitor-opentelemetry-exporter

    directory: /frontend
    schedule:
      interval: weekly

    open-pull-requests-limit: 5

### S3-compatible object stores

The **S3** connection is not AWS-only. Leave **Endpoint URL** blank and it addresses AWS
exactly as before; set it to a store that speaks the S3 API — MinIO, Ceph/RadosGW,
Cloudflare R2, Wasabi, Backblaze B2, SeaweedFS, or an on-prem gateway — and the same
connection, checks and monitors work unchanged.

- **Endpoint URL** — the full base URL including scheme, e.g.
  `https://minio.example.com:9000`. A URL without `http://`/`https://` is rejected at
  save time rather than failing later as an opaque connection error.
- **Addressing style** — `auto` (default), `path` or `virtual`. `auto` uses **path**
  addressing whenever an endpoint is set, which is what MinIO and SeaweedFS require;
  with no endpoint it leaves AWS's default untouched. Override it only if your store
  needs the other form (R2 and Wasabi accept virtual-host addressing).
- **Region** is still required — S3-compatible stores generally ignore it, but the AWS
  SDK requires a value. `us-east-1` is the conventional filler.
- The endpoint must **not** embed a credential (`REDACTED`). Connection
  `config` is stored and returned in plaintext, so a credential there would live outside
  the REDACTED store; it is rejected at save time. Put the key in **Access key ID** and the
  REDACTED in the credential field.
- An `http://` endpoint is accepted (in-cluster MinIO usually has no TLS), but object
  bytes and request signatures then travel **cleartext** — prefer `https://` for anything
  crossing a network you don't control.

fix(rollup): pick a sweep batch once, so it never claims past its limit

The sweep claimed runs with UPDATE … WHERE id IN (SELECT … ORDER BY id
LIMIT n FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED). With runs estimated near-empty, the
planner made that subquery the rescanned inner side of a nested-loop
semi join; each rescan skipped the rows this statement had already
claimed and took the next ones, so one batch could claim the whole
backlog. The batch is now picked in a MATERIALIZED CTE, executed once.

The regression test forces that plan (ANALYZE on the empty table, then
hash/merge/material/sort off) and inserts runs in id order, so the old
statement claims all six runs in the first limit=2 batch.

Fixes #2753

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

Fixes #2753

## Cause: a product bug, not test leftovers
I captured the plan of the failing call inside the `tests/db` + rollup run (`roll_up_pending(limit=2)` → 3):

```
Update on runs
  ->  Nested Loop Semi Join
        ->  Seq Scan on runs                      (rows=1)
        ->  Subquery Scan on "ANY_subquery"       ← rescanned per outer row
              ->  Limit -> LockRows -> Sort -> Seq Scan on runs runs_1
```

`tests/db` leaves `runs` analysed as near-empty, so the planner puts the `LIMIT … FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` subquery on the inner side of a semi join with no Materialize. Each rescan sees the rows this statement already updated as self-modified, skips them, and takes the next `limit`, so the batch keeps walking forward. With runs stored in id order it claims the whole backlog in one statement.

Counts were never wrong (each run is still claimed once and its results added once). What broke is the batch bound: `SWEEP_BATCH` exists to keep a backlog sweep to small transactions, and stale stats on a real deployment could produce the same plan.

## Fix
The batch is picked in a `MATERIALIZED` CTE (`picked`), which runs once. The `UPDATE` matches `id IN (SELECT id FROM picked)`. `_ADD_ONE` is unchanged (`pick=""`).

## Test
`test_a_sweep_batch_never_claims_more_than_its_limit_whatever_the_plan` forces the plan (`ANALYZE runs` while empty, then `enable_hashjoin/mergejoin/hashagg/material/sort = off`) and inserts six runs in ascending id order.
- old statement: `[6, 0, 0, 0]` (3 of 3 runs)
- this branch: `[2, 2, 2, 0]`

The original combination (`tests/db` + rollup + `test_dashboard_one_pass` + the LLM service tests) now passes 604/604 three times in a row. It failed 2 to 3 tests on `main`.

## Siblings checked
The other `SKIP LOCKED` claims (`schedule_dispatch`, `pipeline_baseline`, `workspace_health_service`) are top-level `SELECT … FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED [LIMIT]`, executed once, so they aren't affected.

content.content:
"""Ask the planner whether it CAN use an index, not whether it prefers it on a toss-up (#2545).

On a near-empty table two indexes cost about the same, so which one `EXPLAIN` names depends on
the statistics earlier tests left behind. A test that asserts one particular index was used then
passes alone and fails after the full suite. Dropping the table's other non-unique indexes inside
the test's own transaction (rolled back with it) leaves the planner only that index to choose.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any

from sqlalchemy import text

_RIVALS = text(
    "SELECT other.indexrelid::regclass::text FROM pg_index AS target "
    "JOIN pg_index AS other ON other.indrelid = target.indrelid "
    "WHERE target.indexrelid = CAST(:index AS regclass) "
    "AND other.indexrelid <> target.indexrelid "
    "AND NOT other.indisunique AND NOT other.indisprimary"
)


def drop_rival_indexes(connection: Any, index: str) -> list[str]:
    """Drop every other non-unique index on ``index``'s table, in the open transaction.

    Returns the names dropped. The caller's transaction must be rolled back afterwards, which the

"""Ask the planner whether it CAN use an index, not whether it prefers it on a toss-up (#2545).

On a near-empty table two indexes cost about the same, so which one `EXPLAIN` names depends on
the statistics earlier tests left behind. A test that asserts one particular index was used then
passes alone and fails after the full suite. Dropping the table's other indexes inside the test's
own transaction (rolled back with it) leaves the planner only that index to choose.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any

from sqlalchemy import text

# Each rival, with the constraint behind it if any: a constraint's index is dropped with it.
_RIVALS = text(
    "SELECT other.indexrelid::regclass::text, other.indrelid::regclass::text, con.conname "
    "FROM pg_index AS target "
    "JOIN pg_index AS other ON other.indrelid = target.indrelid "
    "LEFT JOIN pg_constraint AS con ON con.conindid = other.indexrelid "
    "AND con.conrelid = other.indrelid "
    "WHERE target.indexrelid = CAST(:index AS regclass) "
    "AND other.indexrelid <> target.indexrelid AND NOT other.indisprimary "
    "AND (CAST(:unique AS boolean) OR NOT other.indisunique)"
)


def drop_rival_indexes(connection: Any, index: str, *, unique: bool = False) -> list[str]:
    """Drop every other non-unique index on ``index``'s table, in the open transaction; with
    ``unique``, the unique ones too (and the constraint behind each, with what depends on it).
    The primary key always stays.

    Returns the names dropped. The caller's transaction must be rolled back afterwards, which the
    ``db_session`` fixture does.
    """
    rivals = connection.execute(_RIVALS, {"index": index, "unique": unique}).all()
    for rival, table, constraint in rivals:
        if constraint is None:
            connection.execute(text(f"DROP INDEX {rival}"))
        else:
            connection.execute(text(f'ALTER TABLE {table} DROP CONSTRAINT "{constraint}" CASCADE'))
    return [rival for rival, _, _ in rivals]
EOF

def test_the_index_depends_on_client_side_parameter_binding(db_session: Any) -> None:
    """A partial expression index needs CONSTANTS: the planner must prove `kind`/`status`
    imply the index predicate, and `request ->> 'incident_id'` must match the indexed
    expression textually. Under server-side binding those are all parameters, nothing is
    provable, and the query silently falls back to a sequential scan — with the suite green,
    since a wrong plan is still a correct answer.

    `EXPLAIN (GENERIC_PLAN)` (PG16+) plans exactly that case, so assert BOTH halves: the
    generic plan does not reach the index, and the driver actually in use is one that
    interpolates client-side. A psycopg3 swap then turns this from a silent perf regression
    into a failing test (#1979).
    """
    connection = db_session.connection()
    assert_client_side_binding(connection)
    connection.execute(text("SET LOCAL enable_seqscan = off"))
    generic = "\n".join(
        row[0]
        for row in connection.execute(
            text(
                "EXPLAIN (GENERIC_PLAN) SELECT id FROM llm_invocations "
                "WHERE kind = $1 AND status = $2 AND (request ->> $3) = $4 "
                "ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT $5"
            )
        )
    )
    assert _INDEX not in generic, (
        "server-side binding now reaches the index — the client-side-binding caveat "
        f"on this index can be dropped:\n{generic}"
    )

    `ix_runs_suite_created` cannot serve because it leads with `suite_id`.

    `enable_seqscan`/`enable_sort = off` remove the empty-test-table cost preference for a
    scan-then-sort plan; they cannot conjure an ordered path out of an index whose column
    order does not match the ORDER BY — with the index absent the planner sorts anyway.
    """
    connection = db_session.connection()
    connection.execute(text("SET LOCAL enable_seqscan = off"))
    connection.execute(text("SET LOCAL enable_sort = off"))
    plan = _plan(connection, _runs_list_statement())
    assert _RUNS_INDEX in plan, f"the /runs page did not use {_RUNS_INDEX}:\n{plan}"

    assert "ix_runs_created_id" in plan, plan
    assert "runs.suite_id = suites.id" not in plan, plan

- `backend/tests/support/index_plans.py: drop_rival_indexes(connection, index, *, unique=False)`. With `unique=True` it also drops the table's unique indexes; one backed by a constraint goes through `ALTER TABLE … DROP CONSTRAINT … CASCADE`, since `DROP INDEX` refuses a constraint's index. The primary key always stays. Everything happens in the test's transaction, which the `db_session` fixture rolls back.
- Applied with `unique=True` wherever a test asserts that a named index serves the query:

| File | Test | Index |
|---|---|---|
| `orchestration/test_markers.py` | `test_marker_lookups_use_the_expression_index` | `ix_pipeline_runs_marker` |
| `db/test_runs_triggered_by_index_migration.py` | `test_pipeline_run_marker_lookup_still_uses_the_expression_index` | same (was non-unique only) |
| `db/test_llm_invocations_status_index_migration.py` | `test_reaper_equality_predicates_can_use_the_index` | `ix_llm_invocations_status_open` |
| `db/test_llm_invocations_rca_index_migration.py` | `test_narrative_lookup_uses_the_index` | `ix_llm_invocations_rca_incident` |
| `db/test_list_paging_order_indexes_migration.py` | runs, pipeline_runs and incidents list tests | the three page-order indexes |
| `db/test_accessible_suite_filter_plan.py` | `test_runs_list_plan_has_no_row_wise_suite_join` | `ix_runs_created_id` |

## The decision per test, as the issue asked
- **Equality lookups**: the question is whether the index can serve the predicate, so dropping every rival is the right test.
- **Ordering indexes**: the assertion is that the index gives the page order without a sort. A rival can't serve that order (the docstrings say so: with the index absent the planner sorts), so removing rivals keeps the question the same and removes the toss-up.
- **Left alone**: `test_incident_count_is_not_claimed_to_use_the_page_index` and `test_the_index_depends_on_client_side_parameter_binding` assert an index is *not* used. Dropping rivals there would make them pass trivially.

## Why unique ones too
The CI speed-up branch's `-n 4` runs failed both marker tests when the planner picked `uq_pipeline_runs_provider_run`, which the helper spared. `test_markers` also never dropped rivals, so `ix_pipeline_runs_provider_pipeline` could win there.

## Tests
`db/test_index_plans_helper.py`: by default only non-unique rivals go; with `unique=True` the unique constraint goes too and the PK stays. All 69 planner tests in the touched files pass, plus the two new ones.

input.command:
cd frontend && npx prettier --check tests/components/ConnectionForm.test.tsx 2>&1 | tail -1 && npx eslint tests/components/ConnectionForm.test.tsx && cd .. && git add -A && git commit -q -m "test(frontend): type without a timer between keystrokes in ConnectionForm

Every ConnectionForm case types several fields through userEvent, and
each keystroke waited a timer tick. Under coverage on a loaded runner
the long cases (36-character tenant and client ids) crossed vitest's 5 s
default. With delay: null the slowest case goes from 1473 ms to 499 ms
under coverage locally, and the file from 11.4 s to 5.4 s.

Fixes #2471

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>" 2>&1 | grep -E "Failed|rror"; git push -q -u origin HEAD 2>&1 | grep -v "^remote:\|entire"; gh pr create --base main --milestone "v1.3 Week 8 — test & dependency debt, decisions & cycle close" --label no-changelog --title "test(frontend): type without a timer between keystrokes in ConnectionForm" --body "Fixes #2471

All 40 \`userEvent.setup()\` calls in \`tests/components/ConnectionForm.test.tsx\` become \`userEvent.setup({ delay: null })\`, so typing doesn't wait a timer tick per keystroke.

The issue's comment found the margin is file-wide (two different cases crossed 5 s under load), so this fixes the file's cost instead of raising one test's timeout, which would only move the cliff.

| slowest three cases | 795 / 1280 / 1473 ms | 381 / 410 / 499 ms |
| file test time (no coverage) | 11.41 s | 5.39 s |

p='backend/tests/support/index_plans.py'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('''passes alone and fails after the full suite. Dropping the table's other indexes inside the test's
own transaction (rolled back with it) leaves the planner only that index to choose.''','''passes alone and fails after the full suite. Dropping the table's other non-primary indexes (the
unique ones only when asked) inside the test's own transaction, which is rolled back with it, leaves
the planner only that index to choose.''')
s=s.replace('''    "SELECT other.indexrelid::regclass::text, other.indrelid::regclass::text, con.conname "''','''    "SELECT other.indexrelid::regclass::text, other.indrelid::regclass::text, "
    "quote_ident(con.conname) "''')
s=s.replace('''    "AND con.conrelid = other.indrelid "''','''    "AND con.conrelid = other.indrelid AND con.contype IN ('u', 'x') "''')
s=s.replace('''            connection.execute(text(f"DROP INDEX {rival}"))''','''            connection.execute(text(f"DROP INDEX {rival} CASCADE"))''')
s=s.replace('''            connection.execute(text(f'ALTER TABLE {table} DROP CONSTRAINT "{constraint}" CASCADE'))''','''            connection.execute(text(f"ALTER TABLE {table} DROP CONSTRAINT {constraint} CASCADE"))''')

def test_only_non_unique_rivals_go_by_default(db_session: Any) -> None:

def test_unique_rivals_a_foreign_key_depends_on_go_with_it(db_session: Any) -> None:
    """A unique constraint and a constraint-less unique index, each referenced by a foreign key
    (one of them from the same table), need CASCADE; the foreign keys go with them."""

    connection.execute(text("""

            id int PRIMARY KEY, code text, alt text, parent text, tag text,

# Snowflake SQLAlchemy

[![Build and Test](https://github.com/snowflakedb/snowflake-sqlalchemy/actio
- v2.0.0 (Oct 19, 2026)
  - **Breaking changes**
    - Drop SQLAlchemy 1.4 support: the dialect now requires `SQLAlchemy>=2.0.44,<2.1`. SQLAlchemy 2.1.0 removed `sqlalchemy.orm.context.ORMSelectCompileState` and changed other APIs the dialect and async shim import at module load time, so 2.1 is excluded. The internal `snowflake.sqlalchemy.compat` module (SQLAlchemy 1.4/2.0 shim) was removed. Users still on SQLAlchemy 1.4 should pin `snowflake-sqlalchemy<2.0.0`.
    - Require `snowflake-connector-python>=5.0.0` (connector 5.x), which provides the async driver. Connector 4.x is no longer supported.
    - Supported Python versions are now 3.11–3.14 (drop 3.8, 3.9 and 3.10), since connector 5.x itself requires Python 3.11+. Updates `requires-python`, Python classifiers, and mypy/ruff targets accordingly.
    - `enable_structured_type_json` is on by default (see Features); explicitly setting it to `False` restores raw JSON strings and emits a `DeprecationWarning` (SNOW-3942921).
    - Remove the `force_div_is_floordiv` dialect flag. The `/` operator always performs true division (`left / right`) and `//` always performs floor division (`FLOOR(left / right)`). Passing the flag to `create_engine()` now raises `TypeError`. Coming from a release older than 1.11.1, integer `//` previously compiled to plain `/` (true division in Snowflake) under the default flag value; it now floors (GH #756).
- v2.0.0rc2 (Sep 29, 2026)
  - Pin `SQLAlchemy<2.1` (floor remains `>=2.0.44`). SQLAlchemy 2.1.0 removed `sqlalchemy.orm.context.ORMSelectCompileState` and changed other APIs the dialect and async shim import at module load time, which broke `import snowflake.sqlalchemy` outright under the previously unbounded dependency range.
  - Improve stage reference handling in compiled `COPY INTO` and staged-file SQL (CWE-89): `ExternalStage` paths, including sub-paths created with `from_parent_stage`, are rendered safely with escaping when quoting is required. Ordinary bare-path values retain their existing rendering (SNOW-4134196).
  - Fix NULL_IF backslash breakout in COPY FILE_FORMAT options (SNOW-4134195).
  - Support UUID and DECFLOAT values inside `VARIANT` and structured types. Structured type compilers now compile their inner types against the Snowflake dialect, so `ARRAY`/`MAP`/`OBJECT` element, key and field types render consistently with standalone columns. The semi-structured JSON write path serializes `decimal.Decimal` as a JSON string (preserving all 38 DECFLOAT digits, which a JSON number would truncate); reading one back requires an intermediate `::VARCHAR` cast, since Snowflake rejects a direct `TEXT` -> `DECFLOAT` cast on `PARSE_JSON` output. New opt-in `enable_native_uuid` dialect flag (URL parameter or `create_engine(..., enable_native_uuid=True)`) renders SQLAlchemy's generic `Uuid` and `Mapped[uuid.UUID]` as native Snowflake `UUID` instead of `CHAR(32)`, and allows `uuid.UUID` inside semi-structured payloads. Off by default, since enabling it changes the DDL of existing `Uuid` columns (SNOW-4081644).

- v2.0.0rc1 (Sep 14, 2026)
  - **Async support**: the dialect now implements SQLAlchemy's [`asyncio` extension](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/orm/extensions/asyncio.html). Use `create_async_engine()` with the same `snowflake://` URL as the sync dialect — there is no separate `+driver` suffix — to obtain `AsyncEngine` / `AsyncSession` for non-blocking database access.
  - **Breaking change**: require `snowflake-connector-python>=5.0` (connector 5.x), which is what provides the async driver. Connector 4.x is no longer supported.
  - **Breaking change**: raise the minimum supported Python to 3.11 (drop Python 3.10), since `snowflake-connector-python>=5.0.0rc3` itself requires Python 3.11+ (dropped 3.10). Updates `requires-python`, Python classifiers, and mypy/ruff targets accordingly.
  - The dialect now sets `enable_server_session_keep_alive_auto_detection=True` explicitly on new connections. This pins the connector's present default so behaviour stays stable when that default changes, and silences the connector's `FutureWarning`. A value supplied via the URL or `connect_args` still takes precedence.
  - Remove the `force_div_is_floordiv` dialect flag entirely. The `/` operator always performs true division (`left / right`) and `//` always performs floor division (`FLOOR(left / right)`); the flag had no SQL effect. Passing it to `create_engine()` now raises `ArgumentError` (GH #756).

input.command:
gh issue comment 2275 --body "**Week 8 decision (2026-11-28): rolled to the backlog, with one blocker removed and the other restated.**

1. **The mypy plugin: removed in #2773.** Every model is \`Mapped[...]\`, and mypy passes on \`backend/app\` and \`backend/tests\` without the plugin.
2. **snowflake-sqlalchemy: unblocked upstream, but the path is now a driver major.** \`snowflake-sqlalchemy\` 2.1.0 (2026-10-26) allows \`sqlalchemy<2.2\`. It comes through the 2.x line, which requires \`snowflake-connector-python>=5\` (we pin 4.x) and changes runtime behaviour: \`enable_structured_type_json\` defaults to on (VARIANT/OBJECT/ARRAY reads come back as Python objects, not JSON strings) and \`force_div_is_floordiv\` is gone. Those are values crossing the Snowflake driver boundary, and only a live Snowflake run counts as evidence for them, which waits on a cloud test instance (#2224).

Every other dialect we pin already declares a range that admits 2.1: sqlalchemy-redshift 1.0.0 (\`<3\`), sqlalchemy-bigquery 1.18.0 (\`<3\`), sqlalchemy-pytds 1.0.3, pyathena 4.2.1, trino 0.340.0, databricks-sqlalchemy 2.0.10, alembic 1.20.1, and GX 1.17.2 (\`>=1.4\`). Declared ranges are not tested support, so each dialect still needs its lane run on 2.1.

**Next step, when #2224 has a Snowflake account:** one PR moving \`snowflake-connector-python\` 5.x + \`snowflake-sqlalchemy\` 2.1 (still on SQLAlchemy 2.0, which 2.1.0 also allows), live-verified. Then SQLAlchemy 2.1 on its own, with the dependabot ignore removed." >/dev/null && gh issue edit 2275 --milestone "v1.3 Backlog" >/dev/null && echo rolled

I couldn't find an official Docker image for Babelfish for PostgreSQL, either from the babelfish-for-postgresql project or from AWS. Every image I found is maintained by the community.

**Community images:**
- **jonathanpotts/babelfishpg** (Docker Hub), which looks like the most widely used option. It describes itself as a Docker image for Babelfish for PostgreSQL and runs with docker run -d -p 1433:1433 jonathanpotts/babelfishpg. Its build workflow on GitHub fetches the latest release tag from babelfish-for-postgresql/babelfish-for-postgresql, so it should keep up with upstream releases. Data is stored in the /var/lib/babelfish/data volume. To build a different version, the Babelfish version tags are listed at https://github.com/babelfish-for-postgresql/babelfish-for-postgresql/tags.
- **rsubr/postgres-babelfish**, labelled "Postgres Babelfish (Unofficial)". It was last updated over 3 years ago, so it's out of date.
- **ongres/babelfish-on-docker**, which provides Docker templates and Dockerfiles for Babelfish. Its examples use old versions (BABEL_2_1_1__PG_14_3).
- **oxeva/postgresql**, with tags updated into 2026, such as oxeva/postgresql:15.10-20260209-01-babelfish-3.8.0-standard-bookworm.

**Other context from 2026:**
- An April 2026 Evolve Cloud Services blog post describes building a custom image with PostgreSQL 17.5 with Babelfish 5.2.0 running on Amazon Linux, to match an Aurora cluster. Their client didn't want to rely on community-maintained Docker images, so they started from Jonathan Potts' docker-babelfish Dockerfile.
- Babelfish Compass v.2026-06 added support for Babelfish v.6.0.0, which suggests 6.0.0 is a recent Babelfish release.

In short, there's no official image. jonathanpotts/babelfishpg is the usual community choice, and if you need something you control, the common approach is to build your own from its Dockerfile.

"""The harness an up/down migration test runs one revision file through, against the test
session's connection."""

from __future__ import annotations

import importlib.util
from pathlib import Path
from types import ModuleType
from typing import Any

from alembic.migration import MigrationContext
from alembic.operations import Operations
from sqlalchemy import text

from backend.app.db.base import Base

VERSIONS = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "alembic" / "versions"


def load_migration(filename: str) -> ModuleType:
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
        f"_migration_{filename[:12]}", VERSIONS / filename
    )
    assert spec is not None and spec.loader is not None
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return module


def run_migration(db: Any, filename: str, direction: str) -> None:
    """Run ``upgrade`` or ``downgrade`` of one revision file on the session's connection."""
    module = load_migration(filename)
    # The env's target metadata, so the naming convention prefixes constraint names exactly as
    # `alembic upgrade` does in production.
    ctx = MigrationContext.configure(db.connection(), opts={"target_metadata": Base.metadata})
    with Operations.context(ctx):
        getattr(module, direction)()
    db.expire_all()


def table_exists(db: Any, table: str) -> bool:
    return bool(
        db.scalar(
            text(
                "SELECT count(*) FROM information_schema.tables "
                "WHERE table_schema = current_schema() AND table_name = :table"
            ),
            {"table": table},

    )

"""Up/down test for the `f58b4bff54f7_add_users_role` migration (ADR 0033, #740)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import importlib.util
import uuid
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

import pytest
from alembic.migration import MigrationContext
from alembic.operations import Operations
from sqlalchemy import inspect, text
from sqlalchemy.exc import IntegrityError

_MIGRATION_PATH = (
    Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "alembic" / "versions" / "f58b4bff54f7_add_users_role.py"
)


def _load_migration() -> Any:
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("_users_role_migration", _MIGRATION_PATH)
    assert spec is not None and spec.loader is not None
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return module


def _has_role(connection: Any) -> bool:
    return "role" in {c["name"] for c in inspect(connection).get_columns("users")}


def _check_names(connection: Any) -> set[str]:
    return {c["name"] for c in inspect(connection).get_check_constraints("users")}


def test_revision_chain() -> None:
    """The chain, asserted explicitly — a duplicated or misparented revision id
    has bitten this repo twice, and alembic only notices at deploy time.
    """
    module = _load_migration()
    assert module.revision == "f58b4bff54f7"
    assert module.down_revision == "bee3e56e1a5d"


def test_up_down_up(db_session: Any) -> None:
    """down (drop) → up (add) → down (drop) against the live `users` table."""
    module = _load_migration()
    connection = db_session.connection()
    ctx = MigrationContext.configure(connection)
    with Operations.context(ctx):
        assert _has_role(connection)  # baseline from create_all
        assert "ck_users_role_valid" in _check_names(connection)

        module.downgrade()
        assert not _has_role(connection)
        assert "ck_users_role_valid" not in _check_names(connection)

        module.upgrade()
        assert _has_role(connection)
        assert "ck_users_role_valid" in _check_names(connection)

        module.downgrade()
        assert not _has_role(connection)
    db_session.rollback()


def test_upgrade_backfills_an_existing_row_to_member(db_session: Any) -> None:
    """The additive claim, proven on a POPULATED table."""
    module = _load_migration()
    connection = db_session.connection()
    email = f"legacy-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}@example.com"

    ctx = MigrationContext.configure(connection)
    with Operations.context(ctx):
        module.downgrade()
        # A row that predates the column, inserted while the column is absent.
        connection.execute(
            text(
                "INSERT INTO users (id, email, created_at, updated_at) "
                "VALUES (:i, :e, now(), now())"
            ),
            {"i": uuid.uuid4(), "e": email},
        )
        module.upgrade()
        role = connection.execute(
            text("SELECT role FROM users WHERE email = :e"), {"e": email}
        ).scalar_one()
        assert role == "member"
    db_session.rollback()


def test_the_check_constraint_the_migration_creates_actually_enforces(db_session: Any) -> None:
    """The constraint is asserted by NAME above; this asserts it by BEHAVIOUR."""
    module = _load_migration()
    connection = db_session.connection()
    ctx = MigrationContext.configure(connection)
    with Operations.context(ctx):
        module.downgrade()
        module.upgrade()

import re,glob,subprocess
files=subprocess.run("grep -ln MigrationContext backend/tests/db/*.py | xargs grep -L support.migrations | grep -v migration_parity",shell=True,capture_output=True,text=True).stdout.split()
for p in files:
    s=open(p).read()
    m=re.search(r'_MIGRATION_PATH = \(\s*Path\(__file__\)\.resolve\(\)\.parents\[2\] / "alembic" / "versions" / "([^"]+)"\s*\)',s)
    fname=m.group(1)
    s=s[:m.start()]+f'_MIGRATION = "{fname}"'+s[m.end():]
    # _run helper with inline spec loading
    s=re.sub(r'def _run\(db: Any, direction: str\) -> None:\n    spec = importlib.*?\n    db\.expire_all\(\)\n',
             'def _run(db: Any, direction: str) -> None:\n    run_migration(db, _MIGRATION, direction)\n', s, flags=re.S)
    s=re.sub(r'def _load_migration\(\) -> Any:\n    spec = .*?\n    return module\n\n\n','',s,flags=re.S)
    s=s.replace('_load_migration()','load_migration(_MIGRATION)')
    s=re.sub(r'ctx = MigrationContext\.configure\(([^)]*\)?)\)\n(\s+)with Operations\.context\(ctx\):', r'with migration_ops(\1):', s)
    used=[n for n in ("load_migration","migration_ops","run_migration") if re.search(rf'\b{n}\(',s)]
    imp=f"from backend.tests.support.migrations import {', '.join(used)}\n"
    lines=s.split("\n")
    idx=[k for k,l in enumerate(lines) if l.startswith("from backend.")]
    if idx: lines.insert(idx[-1]+1,imp.rstrip())
    else:
        last=max(k for k,l in enumerate(lines) if l.startswith(("import ","from ")) and not l.startswith("from __future__"))
        lines.insert(last+1,""); lines.insert(last+2,imp.rstrip())
    s="\n".join(lines)
    open(p,"w").write(s)
    print(p, fname, used, "MigrationContext" in s.replace("from alembic.migration import MigrationContext",""))
EOF

from __future__ import annotations

import uuid
from typing import Any

import pytest
from sqlalchemy import text
from sqlalchemy.exc import IntegrityError

from backend.tests.support.migrations import run_migration

_MIGRATION = "543b75689c8c_coverage_settings.py"


def _run(db: Any, direction: str) -> None:
    run_migration(db, _MIGRATION, direction)


def _present(db: Any) -> tuple[bool, bool]:
    table = db.scalar(
        text(
            "SELECT count(*) FROM information_schema.tables "
            "WHERE table_schema = current_schema() AND table_name = 'coverage_settings'"
        )
    )
    column = db.scalar(
        text(
            "SELECT count(*) FROM information_schema.columns "
            "WHERE table_schema = current_schema() "
            "AND table_name = 'assets' AND column_name = 'auto_coverage_config'"
        )
    )
    return bool(table), bool(column)


def _asset_written_by_old_code(db: Any) -> uuid.UUID:
    # Raw SQL, naming no `auto_coverage_config`: the row the running release writes.
    asset_id = uuid.uuid4()
    db.execute(
        text("INSERT INTO assets (id, namespace, name) VALUES (:id, 'ns', :name)"),
        {"id": asset_id, "name": f"s.t_{asset_id.hex[:8]}"},
    )
    return asset_id


def test_upgrade_leaves_no_setting_and_no_override(db_session: Any) -> None:
    _run(db_session, "downgrade")  # the fixture schema already has both
    existing = _asset_written_by_old_code(db_session)

    _run(db_session, "upgrade")
    written_after = _asset_written_by_old_code(db_session)

    assert db_session.scalar(text("SELECT count(*) FROM coverage_settings")) == 0
    overrides = db_session.scalars(
        text("SELECT auto_coverage_config FROM assets WHERE id IN (:a, :b)"),
        {"a": existing, "b": written_after},
    ).all()
    assert overrides == [None, None]

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Every pnpm override in frontend/package.json says why it exists, and can say when it can go.

package.json is JSON, so an override can't carry a comment. frontend/pnpm-overrides.json holds
the reason and the direct dependencies that pull the package. With no arguments this fails when
the two files disagree. With --resolve (the dependency sweep; needs the network) it resolves the
manifest again WITHOUT the overrides, in a scratch copy, and names each override whose package
already meets its floor everywhere, i.e. one that can be removed.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import re
import shutil
import subprocess  # nosec B404 — runs pnpm on a scratch copy of our own manifest
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

FRONTEND = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "frontend"
RECORD = FRONTEND / "pnpm-overrides.json"
# A lockfile `packages:` key: `  'name@1.2.3':` or `  name@1.2.3:` (peer suffix in parentheses).
LOCK_KEY = re.compile(r"^  '?((?:@[^/@\s]+/)?[^@\s']+)@(\d+)\.(\d+)\.(\d+)[^:']*'?:$")
FLOOR = re.compile(r">=\s*(\d+)\.(\d+)\.(\d+)")


def _overrides() -> dict[str, str]:
    manifest = json.loads((FRONTEND / "package.json").read_text())
    return dict(manifest.get("pnpm", {}).get("overrides", {}))


def check_record() -> list[str]:
    record = {k: v for k, v in json.loads(RECORD.read_text()).items() if not k.startswith("_")}
    overrides = _overrides()
    problems = [f"{k}: override with no entry in {RECORD.name}" for k in overrides.keys() - record]
    problems += [f"{k}: entry in {RECORD.name} for no override" for k in record.keys() - overrides]
    for key, entry in record.items():
        if not str(entry.get("why", "")).strip() or not entry.get("via"):
            problems.append(f"{key}: needs a non-empty 'why' and 'via'")
    return problems


def _selector(key: str) -> tuple[str, int | None]:
    """`brace-expansion@5` → ("brace-expansion", 5); `@scope/pkg` → ("@scope/pkg", None)."""
    name, sep, major = key.rpartition("@")
    if sep and name and major.isdigit():
        return name, int(major)
    return key, None


def removable() -> list[str]:
    overrides = _overrides()
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as scratch:
        work = Path(scratch)
        manifest = json.loads((FRONTEND / "package.json").read_text())
        manifest.get("pnpm", {}).pop("overrides", None)
        (work / "package.json").write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2))
        shutil.copy(FRONTEND / "pnpm-lock.yaml", work / "pnpm-lock.yaml")
        subprocess.run(  # nosec B603 B607 — fixed argv, pnpm from PATH
            ["pnpm", "install", "--lockfile-only", "--ignore-scripts", "--no-frozen-lockfile"],
            cwd=work,
            check=True,
            capture_output=True,
        )
        resolved: dict[str, list[tuple[int, int, int]]] = {}
        for line in (work / "pnpm-lock.yaml").read_text().splitlines():
            if match := LOCK_KEY.match(line):
                name, *version = match.groups()
                resolved.setdefault(name, []).append(tuple(map(int, version)))  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    gone = []
    for key, spec in overrides.items():
        name, major = _selector(key)
        floor = FLOOR.search(spec)
        versions = [v for v in resolved.get(name, []) if major is None or v[0] == major]
        if floor and all(v >= tuple(map(int, floor.groups())) for v in versions):
            gone.append(f"{key}: resolves to {sorted(versions)} without the override (floor {spec})")
    return gone


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--resolve", action="store_true", help="list overrides no longer needed")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    problems = check_record()
    for problem in problems:
        print(problem, file=sys.stderr)
    if problems:
        return 1
    if args.resolve:
        found = removable()
        print("\n".join(found) if found else "every override is still needed")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

p='CONTRIBUTING.md'

lines[i]=lines[i].rstrip()+" The frontend's `pnpm.overrides` get the same look: after `pnpm install`, `python scripts/check-pnpm-overrides.py --resolve` names each override no dependent needs any more, and any whose upper cap holds a dependent outside its own range; drop or widen those, and keep `frontend/pnpm-overrides.json` in step (CI checks that it is)."

EOF
git add -A && git commit -q -m "chore(frontend): record why each pnpm override exists, and find the stale ones

frontend/pnpm-overrides.json gives each pnpm.overrides entry its
reason (the PR that added it, and the advisory where that PR names one)
and the direct dependencies that pull it. scripts/check-pnpm-overrides.py
fails in CI and pre-commit when the record and package.json disagree.
With --resolve it reads every installed package's declared range for
each overridden package and says which overrides no dependent needs any
more, and which hold a dependent outside its own range with their
upper cap. The weekly quick scan (CONTRIBUTING rule 36) runs it.

Today it names six removable (brace-expansion@5, follow-redirects,
nanoid, postcss, undici, zod@4), and undici's <8 cap holds jsdom 31
(wants ^8.12.3) on 7.x.

    def __init__(self, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, columns: list[ColumnProfile]) -> None:
        self.columns = columns

        monkeypatch.setattr(

"""`kind_detail` reads the keys the monitor producers actually write (#1740).

The evidence card lifts monitor-kind fields out of `observed_value` by name, and each producer
spells those names on its own. These tests run every producer for real and pass its output
through `_kind_detail_layer`, so a rename on either side fails here instead of degrading the card
to nulls. A key the layer reads with a default (`.get(key, default)`) may be absent by design: a
baseline run has no diff yet, a short history has no z-score.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta
from types import SimpleNamespace
from typing import Any

import pytest

from backend.app.datasources import monitors
from backend.app.services import anomaly, schema_drift
from backend.app.services.incident_evidence import MONITOR_KINDS, _kind_detail_layer

NOW = datetime(2026, 11, 28, 12, tzinfo=UTC)


class Reads(dict[str, Any]):
    """An `observed_value` that records which keys the layer reads, and how."""

    def __init__(self, data: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        super().__init__(data)
        self.required: set[str] = set()

    def get(self, key: str, *default: Any) -> Any:  # type: ignore[override]
        if not default:
            self.required.add(key)
        return super().get(key, *default)


def assert_layer_reads_what(kind: str, observed: dict[str, Any] | None) -> None:
    assert isinstance(observed, dict), f"{kind}: the producer wrote no observed_value"
    reads = Reads(observed)
    detail = _kind_detail_layer(
        SimpleNamespace(kind=kind),  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        SimpleNamespace(observed_value=reads),  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    )

    assert detail is not None, f"{kind}: no kind_detail for a monitor-kind result"
    missing = reads.required - observed.keys()
    assert not missing, f"{kind}: kind_detail reads {sorted(missing)}, the producer never writes"


def test_freshness() -> None:
    out = monitors.monitor_outcome(
        monitors.FRESHNESS, scalar=NOW - timedelta(hours=3), config={"column": "ts"}, now=NOW
    )
    assert_layer_reads_what(monitors.FRESHNESS, out.observed_value)


def test_volume() -> None:
    out = monitors.monitor_outcome(monitors.VOLUME, scalar=5, config={"min_rows": 10}, now=NOW)
    assert_layer_reads_what(monitors.VOLUME, out.observed_value)


def test_schema_drift_once_compared() -> None:
    payload = schema_drift.diff_schemas(
        [{"name": "id", "type": "int"}, {"name": "gone", "type": "text"}],
        [{"name": "id", "type": "bigint"}, {"name": "new", "type": "text"}],
    )
    out = monitors.monitor_outcome(monitors.SCHEMA_DRIFT, scalar=payload, config={}, now=NOW)
    assert_layer_reads_what(monitors.SCHEMA_DRIFT, out.observed_value)


def test_anomaly_with_enough_history() -> None:
    params = monitors.anomaly_params({"target_metric": "row_count", "min_points": 3})
    payload = anomaly.build_score_payload(50.0, [10.0, 11.0, 12.0, 10.5], params)
    assert_layer_reads_what(monitors.ANOMALY, payload)


def test_aggregate_with_a_breached_bound() -> None:
    config = {"aggregate": "mean", "column": "amount", "max_value": 10}
    out = monitors.monitor_outcome(monitors.AGGREGATE, scalar=25, config=config, now=NOW)
    assert_layer_reads_what(monitors.AGGREGATE, out.observed_value)


def test_every_monitor_kind_is_covered() -> None:
    """pii_drift's producer needs a profiled database: its contract test is in test_pii_drift."""
    covered = {
        monitors.FRESHNESS,
        monitors.VOLUME,
        monitors.SCHEMA_DRIFT,
        monitors.ANOMALY,
        monitors.AGGREGATE,
        monitors.PII_DRIFT,
    }
    assert MONITOR_KINDS - {"column_profile"} <= covered | {"column_profile"}, sorted(
        MONITOR_KINDS - covered
    )


@pytest.mark.parametrize("kind", ["expectation", "comparison"])
def test_non_monitor_kinds_have_no_detail(kind: str) -> None:
    assert _kind_detail_layer(SimpleNamespace(kind=kind), SimpleNamespace(observed_value={})) is None  # type: ignore[arg-type]

def test_a_column_that_starts_looking_like_pii_fails_until_someone_classifies_it(
    graph: dict[str, Any], monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    """The baseline is fixed (schema_drift's shape): rolling it forward would pass the very next
    run and auto-resolve the incident with the column still unclassified."""
    fake = _Fake(monkeypatch, _profile(contact=_EMAILS, status=_PLAIN))

    def run(check: Check) -> Any:  # one executor per simulated run, as the worker builds it
        return _executor(graph)(check)

    run(graph["check"])  # baseline: {contact}

    steady = run(graph["check"])
    assert steady.skipped is False and steady.success is True and steady.metric_value == 0.0

    fake.columns = _profile(contact=_EMAILS, status=_PLAIN, notes=_EMAILS)
    drifted = run(graph["check"])
    assert drifted.success is False and drifted.metric_value == 1.0
    assert drifted.observed_value is not None
    assert drifted.observed_value["new_columns"] == ["notes"]
    assert drifted.observed_value["known_columns"] == ["contact"]
    assert drifted.observed_value["columns_detected"] == 2
    assert drifted.observed_value["columns_unclassified"] == 2
    assert "baseline_captured_at" in drifted.observed_value

    # Nothing changed, nobody acted: still failing, baseline untouched.
    again = run(graph["check"])
    assert again.success is False and again.metric_value == 1.0
    assert again.observed_value is not None
    assert again.observed_value["new_columns"] == ["notes"]
    row = get_baseline(graph["session"], graph["check"].id)
    assert row is not None and row.baseline == {"columns": ["contact"]}

    # Classifying it in the suite policy clears the condition: the next run passes.
    graph["suite"].column_policy = {"pii_columns": ["notes"]}
    graph["session"].commit()
    cleared = run(graph["check"])
    assert cleared.success is True and cleared.metric_value == 0.0

gh pr create --base main --milestone "v1.3 Week 8 — test & dependency debt, decisions & cycle close" --label no-changelog --title "test: tie kind_detail to the keys each monitor producer writes" --body "Fixes #1740

Took the issue's second option, a contract test, over a shared \`TypedDict\`. The test catches a rename on either side without making five producer modules import a schema module. A \`TypedDict\` would also be erased at runtime, so on its own it wouldn't catch a misspelt string key.

## What
- \`backend/tests/services/test_kind_detail_contract.py\` runs each producer for real: \`monitor_outcome\` for freshness, volume, schema_drift (on a real \`diff_schemas\` payload) and aggregate (with a breached bound), plus \`anomaly.build_score_payload\` with enough history. Each \`observed_value\` goes through \`_kind_detail_layer\` wrapped in a dict that records which keys are read **without** a default. Any of those the producer never writes fail the test. Keys read with a default (\`baseline_captured\`, \`insufficient_history\`, the drift lists) may be absent by design.
- \`test_pii_drift.py\` gets the pii_drift half, through the real executor on that file's profiled-database fixtures, for both the baseline run and a drifted run.
- \`test_every_monitor_kind_is_covered\` fails when \`MONITOR_KINDS\` gains a kind without a contract test.

## Proven
- \`age_hours\` → \`age_h\` in \`_freshness_outcome\`: \`freshness: kind_detail reads ['age_hours'], the producer never writes\`
- \`columns_unclassified\` → \`unclassified\` in the pii_drift executor: \`pii_drift: kind_detail reads ['columns_unclassified'], …\`

Both producers were restored; 70 tests pass across the contract, pii_drift and incident-evidence files.

The MCP \`get_incident\` docstring's prose spelling of the keys (the issue's fourth copy) isn't machine-checkable this way. It names the same keys today.
