Speeds up the two CI jobs that each took over 10 minutes: **Backend — tests** and **Frontend — browser E2E**.

## Backend — tests: parallel with pytest-xdist
- `pytest-xdist==3.8.0` (MIT; its one dependency, execnet, is MIT) in `backend/requirements-dev.txt`. CI runs `pytest backend/tests/ -n 4 --dist loadfile`: four workers, one per runner core, and a test file never splits across workers, so the probe databases and roles a file creates by fixed name never meet another worker's.
- `backend/tests/conftest.py`: each worker gets its own database (`<name>_gwN`, created through the server's `postgres` DB) and its own Redis index. A serial run is unchanged.
- `structlog.configure` is wrapped so tests never cache loggers. Cached loggers hid lines from `capture_logs` depending on which test ran first (26 files use it).
- Checkout uses `filter: blob:none` (it took 64 s with `fetch-depth: 0`); the upgrade-path gate still has every commit and tag.

Two tests depended on running alone:
- `test_trigger_labels.py`: `uuid4()` parametrize ids made each worker collect a different test list, which xdist refuses.
- `test_secrets.py::test_approle_403_relogin_is_compare_and_swap_under_concurrency`: the fake refused every token, so the login count tracked thread scheduling. Now only the cached token is revoked and the test asserts `logins == 2`. **Mutation-checked:** with an unconditional clear in `_forget_token_if_current` it fails 3/3 (8–9 logins for 8 threads).

The parallel runs also surfaced two ordering bugs, fixed in their own PRs: #2768 (a product bug: the rollup sweep's `LIMIT … SKIP LOCKED` claim could take past its batch size) and #2769 (planner tests that a unique rival index could win).

**Local timings** (same machine, `--no-cov`): serial 348 s → `-n 4` **~87 s**. Three consecutive `-n 4` runs after merging `main`: 10515 passed, 178 skipped (the opt-in live lanes), 0 failed, 86–88 s each. CI's serial `pytest` took 677 s in run 46059360413; this PR's run gives the CI number.

## Frontend — browser E2E: the static demo gets its own job
- New job **`frontend-demo`** ("Frontend — static demo (record, build, smoke)") runs the demo record/build/smoke (322 s of the E2E job's time) in parallel with the Playwright specs. It shares the E2E job's services, env and setup steps through YAML anchors, the repo's first. This PR's CI run is what proves the runner accepts them.
- `publish-demo` now `needs: frontend-demo`. Required check names are unchanged.

Not done here: splitting the demo's 69-route walk across pages. The job is now off the critical path, so it waits on measured numbers from this PR's run.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF

content.content:
---
title: API versions
url: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/versioning
description: "When making API requests, you must send an `anthropic-version` request header. For example, `anthropic-version: 2026-10-21`. If you are using the [client SDK](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/overview), it sets this header for you."
---

For any given API version, Anthropic preserves:

* Existing input parameters
* Existing output parameters

However, Anthropic may do the following:

* Add additional optional inputs
* Add additional values to the output
* Change conditions for specific error types
* Add new variants to enum-like output values (for example, streaming event types)

Generally, if you are using the API as documented in this reference, Anthropic will not break your usage.

## Version history

Anthropic recommends using the latest API version whenever possible.

* `2026-10-21`

  * [Migrating to API version 2026-10-21](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/migration-2026-10-21) shows how to upgrade.

  * Available on the Claude API, [Claude Platform on AWS](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws), [Claude Models on Google Cloud (Anthropic managed)](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-models-on-google-cloud/anthropic-managed), [Claude Models on Google Cloud (Google managed)](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-models-on-google-cloud/google-managed), and [Microsoft Foundry](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry). On Amazon Bedrock, it’s available for Claude 4.7 and later models. For earlier Claude models on Bedrock, [keep the API version that you use today](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/migration-2026-10-21#availability).

  * Messages API:

    * A request that places a `document` block directly in an `assistant` message returns a 400 error.
    * Sending a `text` block with a non-empty `citations` array in a `user` message, directly or inside a `search_result` block, returns a 400 error.
    * The `temperature`, `top_p`, and `top_k` request parameters are removed. A request that sends any of them returns a 400 error on every model.

  * Admin API:

    * [RBAC groups](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/beta/organization/rbac_groups/list) no longer return `roles`. Use `role_ids` instead.
    * [RBAC group members](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/beta/organization/rbac_groups/members/list), and the response to removing one, no longer return `group_id`. Use `rbac_group_id` instead.
    * [RBAC roles](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/beta/organization/rbac_roles/list) no longer return `name`. Use `display_name` instead.
    * [Organization](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/organization/rate_limits/list) and [workspace](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/organization/workspaces/rate_limits/list) rate-limit entries, and the response to [setting a workspace’s rate limits](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/organization/workspaces/rate_limits/update), no longer return `group_type`. Use `group.type` instead.
    * [API keys](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/organization/api_keys/list) no longer return `workspace_id`. Use `scope.workspace_id` instead. It holds the ID of the key’s workspace, the Default Workspace included. An all-workspaces key has no `scope.workspace_id`.

  * Claude Enterprise Analytics API:

    * The per-user [usage](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/beta/organization/analytics/user_usage_report/list) and [cost](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/beta/organization/analytics/user_cost_report/list) reports no longer have `actor.email`. Use `actor.email_address` instead.

For any given API version, Anthropic preserves:

* Existing input parameters
* Existing output parameters

However, Anthropic may do the following:

* Add additional optional inputs
* Add additional values to the output
* Change conditions for specific error types

gh pr create --base main --head test/issue-2766-cross-browser-owner-picker --milestone "v1.3 Week 8 — test & dependency debt, decisions & cycle close" --label no-changelog --title "test(e2e): press Enter in the owner picker only once an option is active" --body "Fixes #2766

## Cause
Enter in rc-select picks the **active** option. \`@rc-component/select\` 1.12 marks the first option active in a \`useEffect\` keyed on the option count (\`OptionList.js\`, \"Auto active first item when list length or searchValue changed\"), so there is a render where the option is visible but not yet active. The transfer spec pressed Enter as soon as \`getByText(ANALYST)\` was visible, inside that window. Firefox and WebKit land there more often, so nothing was picked and **Transfer** stayed disabled.

**App or spec?** The spec. A keyboard user reads the result and then presses Enter; the effect has run long before a person can react. So this isn't an accessibility defect.

## Fix
- Both owner-picker specs (transfer, and offboarding's heir picker) wait for \`.ant-select-item-option-active\` with the user's text before pressing Enter.
- The transfer spec asserts **Transfer** is enabled before clicking it, so a miss fails with a clear message instead of a click timeout.

## Evidence
Dispatched the full CI with the weekly lane on this branch: run [46110974530](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/actions/runs/46110974530). \`Playwright E2E\` (Chromium), **\`Cross-browser E2E (Firefox, WebKit)\`** and the OTP lane all passed.

The two WebKit flakes from the issue (\`check-editor.spec.ts:113\`, \`suites.spec.ts:58\`) passed in that run with no change. They passed on retry in the first run too. If they come back on a Monday run, they get their own issue with that run's trace.

from backend.tests.support.migrations import load_migration

_MIGRATION_PATH = (
    Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "alembic" / "versions" / "c4e5a6b7d8f9_add_incidents.py"
)


def _load_migration() -> Any:
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("_incidents_migration", _MIGRATION_PATH)
    assert spec is not None and spec.loader is not None
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return module


def _has_incidents(connection: Any) -> bool:
    return bool(inspect(connection).has_table("incidents"))

def test_downgrade_narrows_and_upgrade_widens_both_value_sets(db_session: Any) -> None:
    db = db_session
    module = load_migration(_FILE)
    assert "'suite'" in _provider_check(db)
    assert "suite:%" in _dedup_predicate(db)

    ctx = MigrationContext.configure(db.connection(), opts={"target_metadata": Base.metadata})
    with Operations.context(ctx):
        module._set_provider_check(module._NO_SUITE)
    _rebuild_index(db, module, module._DEDUP_NO_SUITE)

git checkout -q main && git pull -q --ff-only && git checkout -q -b test/issue-1605-parity-negations && python3 - <<'EOF'
p='backend/tests/db/test_migration_parity.py'
s=open(p).read()
anchor='''def _model_predicates() -> dict[str, str]:'''
new='''# The other polarity flips no literal moves with (#1605): `IN` <-> `NOT IN`, `LIKE` <-> `NOT LIKE`,
# `IS [NOT] DISTINCT FROM`. Postgres rewrites each on read-back (`NOT IN (...)` -> `<> ALL (...)`,
# `NOT LIKE` -> `!~~`, and a one-value `IN` -> `=`), so the positive forms don't line up across the
# two sides; the negations do, and a flip in either direction changes their count.
_NEGATIONS = {
    "NOT IN": re.compile(r"\\bNOT\\s+IN\\s*\\(|<>\\s*ALL\\b|\\bNOT\\s*\\(\\s*[^()]*?\\bIN\\s*\\(", re.I),
    "NOT LIKE": re.compile(r"\\bNOT\\s+I?LIKE\\b|!~~\\*?|\\bNOT\\s*\\(\\s*[^()]*?\\bI?LIKE\\b", re.I),
    "IS DISTINCT FROM": re.compile(r"\\bIS\\s+DISTINCT\\s+FROM\\b", re.I),
    "IS NOT DISTINCT FROM": re.compile(r"\\bIS\\s+NOT\\s+DISTINCT\\s+FROM\\b", re.I),
}


def _negations(sql: str) -> dict[str, int]:
    """How many of each negated operator `sql` carries (only the non-zero ones)."""
    counts = {name: len(pattern.findall(sql)) for name, pattern in _NEGATIONS.items()}
    return {name: n for name, n in counts.items() if n}


''' + anchor
assert s.count(anchor)==1; s=s.replace(anchor,new)
old='''        expected_nulls, actual_nulls = _null_polarities(model_sql), _null_polarities(live[name])'''
add='''        expected_negations, actual_negations = _negations(model_sql), _negations(live[name])
        if expected_negations != actual_negations:
            drift.append(
                f"{name}: model has negations {expected_negations}, database has "
                f"{actual_negations}"
            )
'''
s=s.replace(old, add+old)
s=s.replace('''    """Every literal and every IS [NOT] NULL clause a CHECK or partial-index predicate carries must
    match on both sides — literal-set alone is blind to a bare polarity flip (#1326).
    """''','''    """Every literal, every IS [NOT] NULL clause and every negated operator a CHECK or
    partial-index predicate carries must match on both sides — literal-set alone is blind to a
    bare polarity flip (#1326, #1605).
    """''')
s+='''

@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("model_sql", "live_sql"),
    [
        (
            "status NOT IN ('a', 'b')",
            "((status)::text <> ALL ((ARRAY['a'::character varying, 'b'::character varying])::text[]))",
        ),
        ("NOT (status IN ('a', 'b'))", "((status)::text <> ALL (ARRAY['a'::text, 'b'::text]))"),
        ("triggered_by NOT LIKE 'adf:%'", "((triggered_by)::text !~~ 'adf:%'::text)"),
        ("a IS DISTINCT FROM b", "(a IS DISTINCT FROM b)"),
    ],
)
def test_negations_read_the_same_from_the_model_and_the_database(
    model_sql: str, live_sql: str
) -> None:
    assert _negations(model_sql) == _negations(live_sql) != {}


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("model_sql", "flipped_live_sql"),
    [
        (
            "status IN ('a', 'b')",
            "((status)::text <> ALL ((ARRAY['a'::character varying, 'b'::character varying])::text[]))",
        ),
        ("status NOT IN ('a', 'b')", "((status)::text = ANY (ARRAY['a'::text, 'b'::text]))"),
        ("status IN ('a')", "((status)::text <> 'a'::text)"),
        ("triggered_by LIKE 'adf:%'", "((triggered_by)::text !~~ 'adf:%'::text)"),
        ("a IS DISTINCT FROM b", "(a IS NOT DISTINCT FROM b)"),
    ],
)
def test_a_negation_flip_breaks_equality(model_sql: str, flipped_live_sql: str) -> None:
    """Each pair keeps every literal, so `_literals()` alone passes it."""
    assert _literals(model_sql) == _literals(flipped_live_sql)
    assert _negations(model_sql) != _negations(flipped_live_sql)
'''
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

input.command:
git add -A && git commit -q -m "test: catch NOT IN, NOT LIKE and DISTINCT FROM flips in migration parity

The parity check compared each CHECK and partial-index predicate's
literals and IS [NOT] NULL clauses, so IN <-> NOT IN, LIKE <-> NOT LIKE
and IS [NOT] DISTINCT FROM flips, which move no literal, passed. It now
also compares each predicate's count of negated operators. Postgres
rewrites the positive forms on read-back (a one-value IN becomes =),
so the negations are what lines up across the two sides: NOT IN, <>
ALL, <> and != as one family, NOT LIKE and !~~ as another, and the two
DISTINCT FROM forms.

Flipping the model's _in_check to NOT IN now fails 39 predicates.

Fixes #1605

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>" 2>&1 | grep -E "Failed|rror"; git push -q -u origin HEAD 2>&1 | grep -v "^remote:\|entire"; git push -q -u origin HEAD 2>&1 | grep -v "^remote:\|entire"; gh pr create --base main --milestone "v1.3 Week 8 — test & dependency debt, decisions & cycle close" --label no-changelog --title "test: catch NOT IN, NOT LIKE and DISTINCT FROM flips in migration parity" --body "Fixes #1605

## What
\`test_vocabularies_in_predicates_match_between_model_and_database\` compares a third thing per CHECK / partial-index predicate: \`_negations(sql)\`, the count of each negated operator family.

| Family | Model forms | Postgres read-back forms |
|---|---|---|
| \`NOT IN / <>\` | \`NOT IN (…)\`, \`NOT (… IN (…))\`, \`<>\`, \`!=\` | \`<> ALL (…)\`, \`<>\` (a one-value \`NOT IN\`) |
| \`NOT LIKE\` | \`NOT LIKE\`, \`NOT ILIKE\`, \`NOT (… LIKE …)\` | \`!~~\`, \`!~~*\` |
| \`IS DISTINCT FROM\` / \`IS NOT DISTINCT FROM\` | as written | as written |

**Why negations, not every operator:** Postgres rewrites the positive forms (\`IN\` → \`= ANY\`, and a one-value \`IN\` → \`=\`), so positive counts don't line up across the two sides. Negations do, and a flip in either direction changes their count.

## Tests
- Normalisation: 6 model/read-back pairs read the same (including one-value \`NOT IN\` → \`<>\` and \`!=\` → \`<>\`).
- Flips: 5 pairs whose literal sets are identical (so \`_literals()\` passes them) and whose negations differ.
- **End-to-end mutation:** with \`_in_check\` emitting \`NOT IN\`, the schema test fails on 39 predicates (e.g. \`ck_users_role_valid: model has negations {'NOT IN / <>': 1}, database has {}\`). On the real schema, all 17 tests pass.

Same accepted limitation as \`_literals()\` and \`_null_polarities()\`: not quote-aware, so an operator spelt inside a string literal would count. No current predicate has one.

# DataQ v1.2.0 — retrospective

> Internal document (outside the published site). Written 2026-10-04 at the
> `v1.2.0` close, twelve days before the planned 2026-10-16 end of the eight-week
> cycle (2026-08-22 → 2026-10-04). Companion to [progress-v1.2.md](progress-v1.2.md)
> (the frozen per-PR ledger) and [retro-v1.1.md](retro-v1.1.md) (the retro this one
> builds on).

## What shipped

The cycle's thesis was "DQ intelligence + operability", and both halves landed.

- **Intelligence.** The expectation catalog grew behind a server-side allowlist
  (W2). The `LLMProvider` seam (ADR 0042) carries SQL generation, check
  suggestions and root-cause narratives, all off by default and validator-gated
  (W3–W4). Automated coverage (ADR 0047) creates system-owned suites over the
  asset inventory, proposes rules into a review queue, and reports coverage and
  the false-positive rate on the Dashboard.
- **Engines and datasources.** Per-check engines (ADR 0036): Snowflake DMF and
  Databricks DQX. The engine-generic SQL base (ADR 0045) took PostgreSQL,
  MySQL/MariaDB, Trino, Athena and Redshift; SQL Server, Azure SQL, Synapse and
  Fabric SQL arrived on their own driver decision (ADR 0044); OneLake rides the
  ADLS adapter. Five datasources became eleven.
- **Operability.** Reusable notification channels; the admin area as six routed
  pages with in-app membership (ADR 0043) and guided offboarding; a hash chain
  over the audit log; a pipeline gate a DAG can ask for a verdict (ADR 0046);
  a generated Python client and `dataq` CLI with an API compatibility policy;
  suites as YAML files with validate, drift and apply.
- **Surface quality.** The accessibility pass took the axe baseline from 107
  violations to 0 across every route in both themes. The docs were rebuilt on a
  Diátaxis layout with versioned copies per release. Health scores reached
  assets, connections and dimensions; bulk check actions, a first-run path and
  designed empty states closed the last weeks.
- **MCP.** 46 → 54 tools, with the tool-surface gates declared as data and an
  honesty review on every change to the file.
- **Where it runs.** Our own Azure, AWS, Snowflake and Databricks estate was
  retired on 2026-10-03 after four build-and-verify waves in credential-expiry
  order. The product keeps full cloud support. The prebuilt-image stack became
  production-like: HTTPS from a generated CA, TLS on every internal hop, and
  data and a persistent vault in a directory.

migrations · backend tests 4,180 → **8,536** · frontend 1,012 →
**1,651** · datasources 5 → **11** · MCP tools 46 → **54**.

backend-test:
    name: Backend — tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    # Ephemeral Postgres for DB-backed integration tests (seed/run/endpoint).
    services:
      postgres:
        image: ghcr.io/theurgicduke771/ci-postgres:16-alpine
        env:
          POSTGRES_USER: REDACTED
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: REDACTED
          POSTGRES_DB: REDACTED_test
        ports:
          - 5432:5432
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "pg_isready -U REDACTED"
          --health-interval 5s
          --health-timeout 3s
          --health-retries 10
      # Redis broker for the real-broker E2E (dispatch -> worker round-trip).
      redis:
        # GHCR mirror of redis:7-alpine (#993 rate limits). The :7 tag is a SECURITY
        # gate, not staleness — Redis 8 bundles Vector Sets (unpatched RCE); Dependabot
        # does not watch service images. Read #980 before any bump.
        image: ghcr.io/theurgicduke771/ci-redis:7-alpine
        ports:
          - 6379:6379
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "redis-cli ping"
          --health-interval 5s
          --health-timeout 3s
          --health-retries 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          # The upgrade-path gate below needs the release tags and origin/main: every commit, but
          # file contents only on demand (a blobless clone), which takes seconds, not a minute.
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with:
          python-version: "3.13"
          cache: pip

      - name: Install test deps
        # Single source of truth: runtime + typed subset + test toolchain, all
        # from backend/requirements-dev.txt. pip upgraded for PYSEC-2026-196.
        run: |
          python -m pip install -U pip
          pip install -r backend/requirements-dev.txt

      - name: Dependency licences (rule 40 allowlist over the installed set)
        # Folded in here rather than a new job: this is the one job with requirements-dev.txt
        # installed, and a new job name would need the main ruleset's required-check list edited.
        run: python scripts/check-licenses.py backend

      - name: mypy (tests)
        # The slim `Backend — type check` job mypies backend/app against the typed subset; this
        # gates backend/tests too — run here.
        run: mypy backend/tests/

      - name: pytest
        # TEST_DATABASE_URL enables the db_session fixture; DATABASE_URL + REDIS_URL + DATAQ_E2E
        # together enable the real-broker E2E (test_probe_e2e — DATAQ_E2E is the explicit-opt-in
        # signal conftest.py's DATABASE_URL auto-redirect (#1130) can never set on its own, so this
        # test stays a conscious choice even here).
        env:

        run: pytest backend/tests/ -n 4 --dist loadfile

content.content:
name: Mirror CI service images

# Keep the two containers CI's required test jobs depend on inside GHCR, so a Docker Hub outage or
# an anonymous-pull throttle cannot red a merge gate (#993).

on:
  schedule:
    # Weekly. These are upstream patch streams, not our code — a fortnight-stale
    # mirror is fine, and the tags below are the only thing that pins the version.
    - cron: "0 4 * * 1"
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: mirror-ci-images
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: read
  packages: write

env:
  OWNER: theurgicduke771 # lowercase — GHCR paths are case-sensitive

jobs:
  mirror:
    name: Mirror ${{ matrix.source }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - source: postgres:16-alpine
            target: ci-postgres
          # ⚠ redis:7 IS A SECURITY GATE, NOT A STALENESS ARTEFACT (#980) — changing
          # this tag is a conscious security decision, never a routine bump.
          - source: redis:7-alpine
            target: ci-redis

    steps:
      - name: Refuse a silent major bump
        # A mirror is exactly where a version could drift unnoticed — the CI jobs would keep passing
        # while running a different engine.
        env:
          SOURCE: ${{ matrix.source }}
        run: |
          case "$SOURCE" in
            postgres:16-*) ;;
            redis:7-*) ;;
            *)
              echo "::error::$SOURCE is not a pinned major this repo has agreed to."
              echo "Redis must stay on 7.x (#980 — Redis 8 bundles Vector Sets, an unpatched"
              echo "RCE surface). Postgres must stay on 16 to match compose and production."
              exit 1
              ;;
          esac

      - name: Log in to GHCR
        uses: docker/login-action@v4
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: Copy the manifest list into GHCR
        # `imagetools create` copies by digest — no pull, no rebuild, every architecture preserved.
        env:
          SOURCE: ${{ matrix.source }}
          TARGET: ${{ matrix.target }}
        run: |
          # The mirrored tag is the source's TAG, not its whole reference: `${SOURCE}` is
          # `postgres:16-alpine`, so using it wholesale produced `ci-postgres:postgres:16-alpine`.
          TAG="${SOURCE##*:}"
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if docker buildx imagetools create \
                 --tag "ghcr.io/${OWNER}/${TARGET}:${TAG}" \
                 "docker.io/library/${SOURCE}"; then
              exit 0
            fi
            echo "attempt ${attempt} failed; retrying in $((attempt * 15))s"
            sleep $((attempt * 15))
          done
          echo "::error::could not mirror ${SOURCE} after 3 attempts"
          exit 1

      - name: Show what the mirrored tag now points at
        # The digest is the only proof the copy is the image we meant; printed so
        # a drift is visible in the run log rather than inferred from a green tick.
        env:
          SOURCE: ${{ matrix.source }}
          TARGET: ${{ matrix.target }}
        run: |
          docker buildx imagetools inspect \
            "ghcr.io/${OWNER}/${TARGET}:${SOURCE##*:}" \
            --format '{{ .Name }} -> {{ .Manifest.Digest }}'

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Every pnpm override in frontend/package.json says why it exists, and can say when it can go.

package.json is JSON, so an override can't carry a comment. frontend/pnpm-overrides.json holds
the reason and the direct dependencies that pull the package. With no arguments this fails when
the two files disagree. With --resolve (the dependency sweep; run `pnpm install` first) it reads
every installed package's declared range for each overridden package, and names the overrides
that no range would take below the floor any more, i.e. the ones that can be removed.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

FRONTEND = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "frontend"
RECORD = FRONTEND / "pnpm-overrides.json"
FLOOR = re.compile(r">=\s*(\d+)\.(\d+)\.(\d+)")
CAP = re.compile(r"<\s*(\d+)(?:\.(\d+))?(?:\.(\d+))?")


def _overrides() -> dict[str, str]:
    manifest = json.loads((FRONTEND / "package.json").read_text())
    return dict(manifest.get("pnpm", {}).get("overrides", {}))


def check_record() -> list[str]:
    record = {k: v for k, v in json.loads(RECORD.read_text()).items() if not k.startswith("_")}
    overrides = _overrides()
    problems = [f"{k}: override with no entry in {RECORD.name}" for k in overrides.keys() - record]
    problems += [f"{k}: entry in {RECORD.name} for no override" for k in record.keys() - overrides]
    for key, entry in record.items():
        if not str(entry.get("why", "")).strip() or not entry.get("via"):
            problems.append(f"{key}: needs a non-empty 'why' and 'via'")
    return problems

def scratch_engine(name: str, *, tables: list[Table] | None = None) -> Iterator[Any]:

input.command:
git checkout -q -b test/issue-2737-guard-every-table && python3 - <<'EOF'
p='backend/tests/conftest.py'
s=open(p).read()
old_start=s.index('_LEAK_GUARDED_TABLES = ("audit_events", "audit_chain_state", "audit_chain_checkpoints")')
old_end=s.index('# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Local test-infra visibility (#977)')
new='''def _leak_probe() -> str:
    """One statement naming every model table that holds a committed row (#2623, #2737)."""
    from backend.app.db.base import Base

    return " UNION ALL ".join(
        f"SELECT '{t.name}' WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM {t.name})" for t in Base.metadata.sorted_tables
    )


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def _no_committed_state(request: pytest.FixtureRequest) -> "Iterator[None]":
    """Fail the test that commits rows outside `db_session`'s savepoint (#2623, #2737).

    A session opened through `get_db`/`get_session`, or a `TestClient` call with no `get_db`
    override, commits to the shared test database, and nothing rolls that back: the rows then
    reach whichever later test counts rows, verifies the audit chain or assumes an empty
    workspace, and only in a full-suite run. Every model table is checked, the leaker is named
    here, and the tables are emptied so one leaker does not fail the tests after it. A test that
    commits on purpose is marked `commits_for_real`: its rows are still removed, but it is not a
    failure.
    """
    yield
    engine = _SHARED_ENGINE
    if engine is None:
        return
    from sqlalchemy import text

    with engine.begin() as conn:  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
        # A leaker that still holds a lock must fail here, not hang the run.
        conn.execute(text("SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '10s'"))
        left = sorted(conn.execute(text(_leak_probe())).scalars())
        if left:
            conn.execute(text(f"TRUNCATE {', '.join(left)} CASCADE"))
    if left and request.node.get_closest_marker("commits_for_real") is None:
        pytest.fail(
            f"{request.node.nodeid} left committed rows behind (in {', '.join(left)}); they "
            "survive into later tests. Use the `db_session` fixture (override `get_db` with it) or "
            "delete what the test committed in its own teardown.",
            pytrace=False,
        )


'''
s=s[:old_start]+new+s[old_end:]
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

content.content:
general pass does not look for: a suggestion's rationale described as "up to
  a week old" when it is never re-measured; a neighbour docstring that still
  said a figure was not readable after the tool that reads it landed.
- **Mutation-checking regression tests.** Still the cheapest way to learn a test
  proves nothing. In the last week alone it confirmed the new MCP gate, the
  empty-state guards and the check-ordering tests each fail without their fix.
- **Decisions put to the user early and recorded.** Unclassified checks stay in
  the asset score; rollups are workspace-wide; the OTP response stays uniform;
  LLM suggestions stay on demand. Each one unblocked a week of work and is
  written where the code lives (an ADR or the issue).

## What hurt (do differently)

- **The test environment is blind to privileges and commits.** The W2 deploy
  500ed every audited mutation: the audit chain's seal `UPDATE` ran into the
  append-only `REVOKE`, which tests cannot see because they run as a superuser.
  The same blindness hid access events that were never committed. Both now
  have real-database harnesses, but the lesson is general: a rule enforced by
  the database must be tested as the application's own role.
- **No cloud to verify against.** Since 2026-10-03 the "only a live run is
  evidence" rule cannot be met for Snowflake, Unity Catalog, Azure or AWS.
  Work since then is verified locally and says so; #2224 tracks re-running the
  live batteries once a test instance exists. Until then, a driver-boundary
  change to those four is a known risk, not a verified one.
- **One changelog, one insertion point.** Every PR adds its entry at the top of

# DataQ v1.3.0 — retrospective

> Internal document (outside the published site). Written 2026-11-28 at the
> `v1.3.0` close, one day before the planned 2026-11-29 end of the eight-week
> cycle (2026-10-05 → 2026-11-29). Companion to [progress-v1.3.md](progress-v1.3.md)
> (the frozen per-PR ledger) and [retro-v1.2.md](retro-v1.2.md) (the retro this one
> builds on).

## What shipped

The cycle was scoped as **no net-new features**: build what was already on the
roadmap or filed (Weeks 1–5), then bug fixes and security (Week 6), polish
(Week 7), and debt, decisions and the close (Week 8). One exception was taken on
the maintainer's direction: per-period metrics with yearly seasonality (#2440,
ADR 0048).

- **Coverage and checks (W1).** Zero-config auto-baselines (ADR 0047
  amendment), enable/disable a check without deleting it, profiler-side PII
  detection as a classification source (ADR 0049) and the `pii_drift` monitor
  kind that acts on it.
- **Operating DataQ (W2).** A backup/restore runbook and an upgrade-path gate in
  CI, opt-in usage telemetry that defaults off (ADR 0050), third-party notices
  and an SPDX SBOM in the images and releases, a Helm chart, changelog fragments
  (one file per PR), and the yearly-seasonality work.
- **Datasources (W3).** Google BigQuery and Google Cloud Storage, and an
  object-lock tamper anchor for the audit chain. Eleven datasources became
  thirteen.
- **Product surfaces and integrations (W4–W5).** Suite-on-suite triggers
  (ADR 0051), tags, run comparison, the notification centre, the command palette,
  data contracts on ODCS v3 with import, export and per-clause compliance
  (ADR 0052), a purge path for connection version history, and a reason per
  redacted column. The governance-catalog integration was designed (ADR 0053,
  Proposed) and rolled: no user has named a catalog.
- **Bug fixes and security (W6).** Deleting a check no longer rewrites the
  history of the runs it took part in. Sensitive values are masked on every read
  surface (aggregate min/max, suggested value sets, contract exports, PII-drift
  samples). ADF webhooks enforce freshness. Every SQL engine has a per-query time
  limit.
- **Polish (W7).** MCP tools carry their safety class as annotations and report
  what they can't see. The scheduler and dashboard paths stay flat at a million
  rows, deep paging is keyset, and an index audit covers server-side binding.
  The keyboard and screen-reader audits finished. The docs screenshots and clips
  were re-captured for the v1.3 UI, and a weekly Firefox/WebKit lane was added.
- **Debt and decisions (W8).** Below under "Week 8".

**By the numbers:** 264 squash-merged commits · 139 issues closed across the
eight weekly milestones (W6 36, W7 45, W8 28 at the time of writing) · **6 new
ADRs** (0048–0053) · 19 migrations · backend tests 8,536 → **10,693** collected ·
frontend 1,651 → **2,069** · datasources 11 → **13** · MCP tools 54 → **59**.

### Week 8

- **Two order-dependent failures were product bugs.** The results-rollup sweep
  claimed runs with `UPDATE … WHERE id IN (SELECT … LIMIT n FOR UPDATE SKIP
  LOCKED)`. With stale statistics the planner rescanned that subquery per row, and
  each rescan skipped what the statement had already claimed, so one batch could
  take the whole backlog (#2753). Planner tests failed when a unique rival index
  won the toss-up (#2739).
- **CI speed-up.** Backend tests in parallel (pytest-xdist, a database and Redis
  index per worker), and the static demo in its own job (#2789).
- **Dependencies.** Vitest 5 with jest-dom 8, anthropic 2.x (checked against
  the 2026-10-21 API version: none of the removed parameters are sent),
  fastmcp 4.2, the SQLAlchemy mypy plugin dropped. snowflake-connector 5 is held:
  it moves with snowflake-sqlalchemy 2.x, which changes how VARIANT values come
  back, and needs a live Snowflake run (#2275).
- **Test debt.** The migration tests run through one harness that applies the
  production naming convention. Migration parity catches `NOT IN` / `NOT LIKE` /
  `DISTINCT FROM` flips. A contract test ties the evidence card to what each
  monitor writes, a parity test holds the suite import and export models
  together, the S3 tests ignore the developer's AWS config, and every pnpm
  override records why it exists, with a sweep that names the stale ones.

## What worked (keep doing)

- **Asking why a flake flakes.** Both Week 8 "flakes" that blocked the CI
  speed-up had a cause worth knowing. Capturing the real plan of the failing
  statement (`EXPLAIN` from inside the failing run) turned "leftover rows?" into
  a product fix and a deterministic regression test in an hour.
- **Mutation-checking, every time.** Each regression test this week was run
  against the unfixed code first: the rollup claim (`[6, 0, 0, 0]` before the
  fix), the CAS login test, the migration naming test, the parity negations (39
  predicates fail when `_in_check` flips), the evidence-card contract, the
  override record. One of those caught a bug in the fix itself (the sweep read
  zod's `^3.25.0 || ^4.0.0` as major 3).
- **Reviews on every PR, findings always dispositioned.** The Week 8 reviews
  found three migration tests the first pass missed, nine problems in the
  override sweep (four would have called a security floor removable), and the
  landing page's README twin. Each ended fixed, filed or recorded as benign with
  the reason.
- **Decisions recorded where the work lives.** SQLAlchemy 2.1, Babelfish and the
  five cloud- or person-gated items each got a comment saying what was checked,
  what it waits on and the trigger to pick it up.

## What hurt (do differently)

- **Week 7 closed six days late.** It held 45 issues against a plan of about a
  dozen. Week 6 (36) went the same way. The v1.2 retro said to keep a weekly
  milestone to its planned rows; it didn't happen. Unplanned work that ships in
  a week still belongs in the backlog milestone.
- **CI was the bottleneck at the end.** Backend tests and the E2E job each took
  more than 10 minutes, and with 18 PRs open at once (11 of them Dependabot's)
  the runners queued for most of the afternoon. The parallel backend run cuts
  the first. The second needs measuring once the demo job runs on its own.
- **A test that passes for the wrong reason.** The first three parallel runs
  "passed" in a worktree that had no `.env`, so 3,598 database tests were
  skipped. Read the skip count, not just the red count.
- **The ledger drifted again.** The Week 8 table still listed seven items that
  closed in Week 7 sessions. Update the tracker when an item closes, not at the
  week's end.
- **Dependabot lockfile PRs conflict serially.** Each frontend bump conflicts in
  `pnpm-lock.yaml` once the one before it merges. Group the frontend dev
  dependencies in `dependabot.yml`, or batch them into one PR.
- **First pushes of new branches failed** about half the time with a bare
  "remote rejected" while the checkpoint branch pushed alongside. A retry always
  worked. Worth a look in the tooling, not the repo.

## Decisions of record

- **SQLAlchemy 2.1 waits on a live Snowflake run** (#2275, 2026-11-28): the mypy
  plugin is gone; the remaining path is snowflake-connector 5 +
  snowflake-sqlalchemy 2.x, and snowflake-connector majors are ignored in
  `dependabot.yml` until then.
- **Babelfish as the SQL Server stand-in** is a self-built image from a pinned
  upstream tag, never a single-maintainer image (#2312).
- **A conformance claim needs a person at the screen reader** (#2520): no
  automated or agent pass counts.
- **The governance catalog waits for a user to name one** (ADR 0053 Proposed,
  #1690).
- **[conda → uv: the maintainer's call, recorded at the close.]**

## Final verification before the tag

- [CI on `main` at the close commit; zero open PRs once the close-out merges.]
- Weeks 1–7 closed with 0 open; Week 8 closes with the tag.
- Backend 10,693 tests collected (10,515 passed and 178 opt-in live lanes skipped
  in three consecutive parallel runs); frontend 2,069 passed.
- `packages/dataq-client` at `1.3.0`, matching the tag.
- **Not verified:** anything against a live Snowflake, Unity Catalog, Azure or
  AWS, BigQuery or GCS since 2026-10-03 (#2224). BigQuery and GCS were
  verified on their emulators only.

## What rolls (explicitly, never silently)

- **[N] open issues** in `v1.3 Backlog` carry into v1.4 planning.
- **Waiting on a cloud instance (#2224):** the Snowflake and Unity Catalog live
  lanes, the Azure stack's live plan, #2275, #2575, SQL Server's Entra, Fabric
  and ODBC legs.
- **Waiting on a person or a third party:** #2520 (manual screen-reader pass),
  #1708 (external pen test), #732 (listing decisions or a hosted offer).
- **Filed this week:** #2772 (one keystroke-timer-free `userEvent` setup for
  every form test).

three audit tables. A test that commits for real (or an unmarked

in a single statement), names the leaker and the tables, and empties
them with TRUNCATE … CASCADE; commits_for_real tests are cleaned the
same way without failing.

def _per_worker_redis(url: str | None) -> str | None:
    """Each worker on its own Redis database (the base index plus the worker number), so rate
    limits, throttles and broker keys one worker sets are not another worker's state."""
    if not url or not XDIST_WORKER:
        return url
    from urllib.parse import urlsplit, urlunsplit

    index = (base + int(XDIST_WORKER.removeprefix("gw")) + 1) % 16

run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - &e2e-install-browsers
        name: Install Playwright browser
        working-directory: frontend
        # Split the browser download from its OS deps (#704). The weekly lane adds Firefox and WebKit.
        env:
          BROWSERS: ${{ (github.event_name == 'schedule' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch') && 'chromium firefox webkit' || 'chromium' }}
        run: |
          pnpm exec playwright install $BROWSERS
          sudo rm -f /etc/apt/sources.list.d/*microsoft* /etc/apt/sources.list.d/*azure* || true
          echo 'Acquire::http::Timeout "30";' | sudo tee /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/99ci-timeout >/dev/null
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            # #1484: a stalled apt mirror hangs rather than exits non-zero, which the retry loop
            # below can't detect on its own.
            if timeout 300 pnpm exec playwright install-deps $BROWSERS; then ok=1; break; fi
            # #2320: the signal stops at sudo's `sh -c`, so apt-get survives it and
            # the orphan holds the dpkg lock against every retry.
            sudo pkill -x apt-get || true
            timeout 60 bash -c 'while sudo fuser /var/lib/dpkg/lock-frontend >/dev/null 2>&1; do sleep 2; done' || true
            sudo dpkg --configure -a || true
            echo "playwright install-deps attempt $attempt failed; retrying in 5s…"; sleep 5
          done
          [ -n "${ok:-}" ] || { echo "playwright install-deps failed after 3 attempts"; exit 1; }

      - name: Playwright E2E
  frontend-demo:
    name: Frontend — static demo (record, build, smoke)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    # The published demo (#2419), recorded from a seeded stack of its own so it runs beside the
    # browser E2E job instead of before its specs. Same stack as that job: the anchors below.
    services: *e2e-services
    env: *e2e-env
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - *e2e-setup-python
      - *e2e-install-backend
      - *e2e-openbao
      - *e2e-seed
      - *e2e-api
      - *e2e-setup-pnpm
      - *e2e-setup-node
      - *e2e-install-frontend
      - *e2e-install-browsers

      # ── Static demo (#2419) ────────────────────────────────────────────── Never committed:
      # every run records the API responses behind each route, builds the demo and drives the
      # built files with no API, so a change that breaks the published demo fails here.
      - name: Static demo — record, build, smoke
        working-directory: frontend
        env:
          VITE_API_PROXY_TARGET: http://localhost:8000
        run: |
          pnpm demo:capture
          pnpm demo:build
          pnpm demo:smoke

      - name: Upload the static demo
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: demo-site
          path: frontend/dist-demo/
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 7

  publish-demo:
    name: Publish the static demo
    # Every push to main republishes the demo that frontend-demo just recorded and built (#2419).
    # The build is kept as the single commit of the `demo-site` branch — force-pushed, so it
    # never accumulates history — and docs.yml, the one Pages deployer, puts it at /demo/.
    needs: frontend-demo
    if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    permissions:

I reviewed PR 2793 and found four problems, two of which give wrong results in normal use. On a throwaway table in the local Postgres I confirmed how Postgres actually stores and returns these negated forms. Both the false failure and the missed flip are shown in the failure scenario. The test input at line 368 uses `(a IS NOT DISTINCT FROM b)`, which Postgres never returns, so this is hidden.   },

content.thinking: I'm rewriting `_negations` to count column-and-family pairs so it catches negations that move between clauses, and the tests now use real Postgres constraints.

input.command:
git checkout -q test/issue-1605-parity-negations && python3 - <<'EOF'
p='backend/tests/db/test_migration_parity.py'
s=open(p).read()
start=s.index('# The other polarity flips no literal moves with (#1605)')
end=s.index('def _model_predicates() -> dict[str, str]:')
new='''# The other polarity flips no literal moves with (#1605): `IN` <-> `NOT IN`, `LIKE` <-> `NOT LIKE`,
# `IS [NOT] DISTINCT FROM`, `SIMILAR TO`. Postgres rewrites each on read-back: `NOT IN (...)` ->
# `<> ALL (...)`, a one-value `NOT IN` -> `<>`, `NOT LIKE` -> `!~~`, `NOT (s IN (...))` ->
# `NOT ((s)::text = ANY (...))`, `a IS NOT DISTINCT FROM b` -> `NOT (a IS DISTINCT FROM b)`,
# `NOT SIMILAR TO` -> `!~ similar_to_escape(...)`. The positive forms don't line up across the two
# sides (a one-value `IN` comes back as `=`), so the negations are compared, as (column, family)
# pairs so a negation that moves from one column to another is seen too. Not covered: `NOT
# BETWEEN`, which comes back as two comparisons; no predicate uses it.
_COLUMN = r"\\(?\\s*([a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*)\\s*\\)?(?:::[a-zA-Z_ ]+?(?:\\[\\])?)?\\s*"
_NEGATED_OPERATOR = re.compile(
    _COLUMN
    + r"(?P<op>NOT\\s+IN\\s*\\(|<>|!=|NOT\\s+I?LIKE\\b|!~~\\*?|IS\\s+NOT\\s+DISTINCT\\s+FROM\\b"
    r"|NOT\\s+SIMILAR\\s+TO\\b|!~\\s+similar_to_escape)",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
_NOT_WRAPPED = re.compile(
    r"\\bNOT\\s*\\(\\s*" + _COLUMN
    + r"(?P<op>=\\s*ANY\\b|IN\\s*\\(|=|~~\\*?|I?LIKE\\b|IS\\s+DISTINCT\\s+FROM\\b|SIMILAR\\s+TO\\b"
    r"|~\\s+similar_to_escape)",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)


def _family(op: str) -> str:
    op = " ".join(op.upper().split())
    if "DISTINCT" in op:
        return "IS NOT DISTINCT FROM"
    if "SIMILAR" in op or op.startswith(("!~ ", "~ ")):
        return "NOT SIMILAR TO"
    if "LIKE" in op or "~~" in op:
        return "NOT LIKE"
    return "NOT IN / <>"


def _negations(sql: str) -> dict[tuple[str, str], int]:
    """How many negated operators `sql` applies, per (column, family)."""
    counts: dict[tuple[str, str], int] = {}
    for pattern in (_NEGATED_OPERATOR, _NOT_WRAPPED):
        for match in pattern.finditer(sql):
            key = (match.group(1).lower(), _family(match.group("op")))
            counts[key] = counts.get(key, 0) + 1
    return counts


'''
s=s[:start]+new+s[end:]
# replace the two old pure-text tests with DB-backed ones
ts=s.index('@pytest.mark.parametrize(\n    ("model_sql", "live_sql"),')
s=s[:ts]+'''_FORMS = [
    "s NOT IN ('a', 'b')",
    "NOT (s IN ('a', 'b'))",
    "s NOT IN ('a')",
    "n != ''",
    "s NOT LIKE 'x%'",
    "s NOT ILIKE 'x%'",
    "NOT (s LIKE 'x%')",
    "a IS NOT DISTINCT FROM b",
    "s NOT SIMILAR TO 'x%'",
]
_FLIPS = [
    ("s IN ('a', 'b')", "s NOT IN ('a', 'b')"),
    ("s IN ('a')", "s NOT IN ('a')"),
    ("s LIKE 'x%'", "s NOT LIKE 'x%'"),
    ("a IS DISTINCT FROM b", "a IS NOT DISTINCT FROM b"),
    ("s SIMILAR TO 'x%'", "s NOT SIMILAR TO 'x%'"),
    # The negation moves from one column to another; both sides carry one.
    ("n <> 'a' AND s IN ('b', 'c')", "n = 'a' AND s NOT IN ('b', 'c')"),
]


def _as_postgres_returns_it(db_session: Any, predicate: str) -> str:
    """The predicate as Postgres stores and returns it: a real CHECK on a scratch table."""
    connection = db_session.connection()
    connection.execute(text("CREATE TEMP TABLE IF NOT EXISTS neg_t (s varchar(20), a int, b int, n text)"))
    connection.execute(text("ALTER TABLE neg_t DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS neg_c"))
    connection.execute(text(f"ALTER TABLE neg_t ADD CONSTRAINT neg_c CHECK ({predicate})"))
    return str(
        connection.execute(
            text("SELECT pg_get_constraintdef(oid) FROM pg_constraint WHERE conname = 'neg_c'")
        ).scalar_one()
    )


@pytest.mark.parametrize("model_sql", _FORMS)
def test_negations_read_the_same_from_the_model_and_the_database(
    db_session: Any, model_sql: str
) -> None:
    live = _as_postgres_returns_it(db_session, model_sql)
    assert _negations(model_sql) == _negations(live) != {}, live


@pytest.mark.parametrize(("model_sql", "migrated_sql"), _FLIPS)
def test_a_negation_flip_breaks_equality(
    db_session: Any, model_sql: str, migrated_sql: str
) -> None:
    """Each pair keeps every literal, so `_literals()` alone passes it."""
    live = _as_postgres_returns_it(db_session, migrated_sql)
    assert _literals(model_sql) == _literals(live), live
    assert _negations(model_sql) != _negations(live), live
'''
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

#: The session's engine while it is up, for the leak guard below.
_SHARED_ENGINE: object | None = None


#: Tables whose committed rows leak into every later test: the audit chain is one shared head, so
#: a leftover row (or a head whose event a later test deleted) breaks every test that verifies it.
def _leak_probe() -> str:
    """One statement naming every model table that holds a committed row (#2623, #2737)."""
    from backend.app.db.base import Base

    return " UNION ALL ".join(
        f"SELECT '{t.name}' WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM {t.name})"
        for t in Base.metadata.sorted_tables
    )


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def _no_committed_state(request: pytest.FixtureRequest) -> "Iterator[None]":
    """Fail the test that commits rows outside `db_session`'s savepoint (#2623, #2737).

    A session opened through `get_db`/`get_session`, or a `TestClient` call with no `get_db`
    override, commits to the shared test database, and nothing rolls that back: the rows then
    reach whichever later test counts rows, verifies the audit chain or assumes an empty
    workspace, and only in a full-suite run. Every model table is checked, the leaker is named
    here, and the tables are emptied so one leaker does not fail the tests after it. A test that
    commits on purpose is marked `commits_for_real`: its rows are still removed, but it is not a
    failure.
    """
    yield
    engine = _SHARED_ENGINE
    if engine is None:
        return
    from sqlalchemy import text

    with engine.begin() as conn:  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
        # A leaker that still holds a lock must fail here, not hang the run.
        conn.execute(text("SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '10s'"))
        left = sorted(conn.execute(text(_leak_probe())).scalars())
        if left:
            conn.execute(text(f"TRUNCATE {', '.join(left)} CASCADE"))
    if left and request.node.get_closest_marker("commits_for_real") is None:
        pytest.fail(
            f"{request.node.nodeid} left committed rows behind (in {', '.join(left)}); they "
            "survive into later tests. Use the `db_session` fixture (override `get_db` with it) or "
            "delete what the test committed in its own teardown.",
            pytrace=False,
        )

"""`kind_detail` reads the keys the monitor producers actually write (#1740).

The evidence card lifts monitor-kind fields out of `observed_value` by name, and each producer
spells those names on its own. These tests run every producer for real and pass its output
through `_kind_detail_layer`, so a rename on either side fails here instead of degrading the card
to nulls or to an empty list that reads as "nothing changed". Each case is a branch where the
producer must write every key the layer reads, apart from the ones named as absent by design
there (a compared schema-drift run has no `baseline_captured`, a scored anomaly no
`insufficient_history`).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Callable
from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta
from types import SimpleNamespace
from typing import Any

import pytest

from backend.app.datasources import monitors
from backend.app.services import anomaly, schema_drift
from backend.app.services.incident_evidence import MONITOR_KINDS, _kind_detail_layer

NOW = datetime(2026, 11, 28, 12, tzinfo=UTC)


class Reads(dict[str, Any]):
    """An `observed_value` that records every key the layer reads, however it reads it."""

    def __init__(self, data: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        super().__init__(data)
        self.read: set[str] = set()

    def get(self, key: str, *default: Any) -> Any:
        self.read.add(key)
        return super().get(key, *default)

    def __getitem__(self, key: str) -> Any:
        self.read.add(key)
        return super().__getitem__(key)

    def __contains__(self, key: object) -> bool:
        if isinstance(key, str):
            self.read.add(key)
        return super().__contains__(key)


def assert_layer_reads_what(
    kind: str, observed: dict[str, Any] | None, *, absent_by_design: frozenset[str] = frozenset()
) -> None:
    assert isinstance(observed, dict), f"{kind}: the producer wrote no observed_value"
    reads = Reads(observed)
    detail = _kind_detail_layer(
        SimpleNamespace(kind=kind),  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        SimpleNamespace(observed_value=reads),  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    )

    assert detail is not None, f"{kind}: no kind_detail for a monitor-kind result"
    assert reads.read, f"{kind}: the layer read no key, so this test checks nothing"
    missing = reads.read - observed.keys() - absent_by_design
    assert not missing, f"{kind}: kind_detail reads {sorted(missing)}, the producer never writes"


def _freshness() -> None:
    out = monitors.monitor_outcome(
        monitors.FRESHNESS, scalar=NOW - timedelta(hours=3), config={"column": "ts"}, now=NOW
    )
    assert_layer_reads_what(monitors.FRESHNESS, out.observed_value)


def _volume() -> None:
    out = monitors.monitor_outcome(monitors.VOLUME, scalar=5, config={"min_rows": 10}, now=NOW)
    assert_layer_reads_what(monitors.VOLUME, out.observed_value)


def _schema_drift() -> None:
    payload = schema_drift.diff_schemas(
        [{"name": "id", "type": "int"}, {"name": "gone", "type": "text"}],
        [{"name": "id", "type": "bigint"}, {"name": "new", "type": "text"}],
    )
    out = monitors.monitor_outcome(monitors.SCHEMA_DRIFT, scalar=payload, config={}, now=NOW)
    assert_layer_reads_what(
        monitors.SCHEMA_DRIFT, out.observed_value, absent_by_design=frozenset({"baseline_captured"})
    )


def _anomaly() -> None:
    params = monitors.anomaly_params({"target_metric": "row_count", "min_points": 3})
    payload = anomaly.build_score_payload(50.0, [10.0, 11.0, 12.0, 10.5], params)
    assert_layer_reads_what(
        monitors.ANOMALY, payload, absent_by_design=frozenset({"insufficient_history"})
    )


def _aggregate() -> None:
    config = {"aggregate": "mean", "column": "amount", "max_value": 10}
    out = monitors.monitor_outcome(monitors.AGGREGATE, scalar=25, config=config, now=NOW)
    assert_layer_reads_what(monitors.AGGREGATE, out.observed_value)


#: One producer case per monitor kind. pii_drift's producer needs a profiled database, so its
#: case lives in `test_pii_drift.py::test_kind_detail_reads_the_keys_this_executor_writes`.
PRODUCERS: dict[str, Callable[[], None] | None] = {
    monitors.FRESHNESS: _freshness,
    monitors.VOLUME: _volume,
    monitors.SCHEMA_DRIFT: _schema_drift,
    monitors.ANOMALY: _anomaly,
    monitors.AGGREGATE: _aggregate,
    monitors.PII_DRIFT: None,
}


@pytest.mark.parametrize("kind", [k for k, case in PRODUCERS.items() if case is not None])
def test_kind_detail_reads_what_the_producer_writes(kind: str) -> None:
    case = PRODUCERS[kind]
    assert case is not None
    case()


def test_every_monitor_kind_has_a_producer_case() -> None:
    assert set(PRODUCERS) == set(MONITOR_KINDS), "a new monitor kind needs a producer case here"


def test_a_renamed_defaulted_key_is_caught() -> None:
    """`added` is read with a default; a compared run that lacks it must still fail."""
    payload = schema_drift.diff_schemas([{"name": "a", "type": "int"}], [])
    payload["columns_added"] = payload.pop("added")
    out = monitors.monitor_outcome(monitors.SCHEMA_DRIFT, scalar=payload, config={}, now=NOW)
    with pytest.raises(AssertionError, match="added"):
        assert_layer_reads_what(
            monitors.SCHEMA_DRIFT,
            out.observed_value,
            absent_by_design=frozenset({"baseline_captured"}),
        )


@pytest.mark.parametrize("kind", ["expectation", "comparison"])
def test_non_monitor_kinds_have_no_detail(kind: str) -> None:
    check, result = SimpleNamespace(kind=kind), SimpleNamespace(observed_value={})
    assert _kind_detail_layer(check, result) is None  # type: ignore[arg-type]

"""`kind_detail` reads the keys the monitor producers actually write (#1740).

The evidence card lifts monitor-kind fields out of `observed_value` by name, and each producer
spells those names on its own. These tests run every producer for real and pass its output
through `_kind_detail_layer`, so a rename on either side fails here instead of degrading the card
to nulls. A key the layer reads with a default (`.get(key, default)`) may be absent by design: a
baseline run has no diff yet, a short history has no z-score.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta
from types import SimpleNamespace
from typing import Any

import pytest

from backend.app.datasources import monitors
from backend.app.services import anomaly, schema_drift
from backend.app.services.incident_evidence import MONITOR_KINDS, _kind_detail_layer

NOW = datetime(2026, 11, 28, 12, tzinfo=UTC)


class Reads(dict[str, Any]):
    """An `observed_value` that records which keys the layer reads, and how."""

    def __init__(self, data: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        super().__init__(data)
        self.required: set[str] = set()

    def get(self, key: str, *default: Any) -> Any:
        if not default:
            self.required.add(key)
        return super().get(key, *default)


def assert_layer_reads_what(kind: str, observed: dict[str, Any] | None) -> None:
    assert isinstance(observed, dict), f"{kind}: the producer wrote no observed_value"
    reads = Reads(observed)
    detail = _kind_detail_layer(
        SimpleNamespace(kind=kind),  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        SimpleNamespace(observed_value=reads),  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    )

    assert detail is not None, f"{kind}: no kind_detail for a monitor-kind result"
    missing = reads.required - observed.keys()
    assert not missing, f"{kind}: kind_detail reads {sorted(missing)}, the producer never writes"

    out = monitors.monitor_outcome(
        monitors.FRESHNESS, scalar=NOW - timedelta(hours=3), config={"column": "ts"}, now=NOW
    )
    assert_layer_reads_what(monitors.FRESHNESS, out.observed_value)

N=$(gh issue create --label "bug,priority/P3" --milestone "v1.3 Week 8 — test & dependency debt, decisions & cycle close" --title "incident evidence: a column-profile anomaly's kind_detail always shows mean and stddev as null" --body "Found by the review of #2788 (#1740's contract test).

\`incident_evidence._kind_detail_layer\` reads \`z_score\`, \`mean\`, \`stddev\` and \`insufficient_history\` for every \`anomaly\` check. An anomaly check with \`target_metric: column_profile\` writes a different payload (\`backend/app/services/anomaly.py\`, the column-profile scorer): \`z_score\` (the worst series) and \`deviations\` (per column and metric: \`value\`, \`mean\`, \`z_score\`), but no top-level \`mean\` or \`stddev\`.

**Effect:** every column-profile anomaly incident's card has \`kind_detail.mean = null\` and \`stddev = null\`, and never says which column deviated. That's null standing for \"not applicable to this shape\", which reads as \"unknown\", and the one field that answers the question (\`deviations\`) isn't lifted. The MCP \`get_incident\` docstring names only \`z_score\`/\`insufficient_history\` for anomaly.

**Fix:** for a column-profile anomaly, lift \`z_score\`, \`insufficient_history\` and the reported \`deviations\` instead of \`mean\`/\`stddev\`, say so in the \`get_incident\` docstring, and add the column-profile producer to the \`kind_detail\` contract test." | tail -1); echo $N

Stacked on #2788 (it extends that PR's contract test); merge after it.

## Bug
\`_kind_detail_layer\` read \`z_score\`, \`mean\` and \`stddev\` for every \`anomaly\` check. The column-profile scorer (\`anomaly.score_column_profile\`) writes \`z_score\` (the worst series) and \`deviations\` (per column and metric: \`value\`, \`mean\`, \`z_score\`) and no top-level \`mean\`/\`stddev\`. So every column-profile anomaly incident showed \`mean: null, stddev: null\`, a null meaning \"not this shape\" that reads as \"unknown\", and never named the column.

## Fix
- For \`target_metric == column_profile\`, \`kind_detail\` is \`{z_score, deviations, insufficient_history}\`. Other anomaly checks are unchanged.
- The \`get_incident\` MCP docstring says a column-profile anomaly carries \`deviations\` instead of a mean and stddev. The generated docs reference is unchanged (it carries only each tool's summary).
- The \`kind_detail\` contract test's anomaly case also runs \`score_column_profile\`. **On the old layer it fails:** \`anomaly: kind_detail reads ['mean', 'stddev'], the producer never writes\`.

Redaction: \`deviations\` holds null percentages and distinct counts per column, aggregates rather than cell values (unlike an aggregate min/max), and \`failing_result.observed_value\` already carries the same list.
